1
陳訓
Chen Xun
2
陳訓，字道元，曆陽人。 少好秘學，天文、算曆、陰陽、占候無不畢綜，尤善風角。 孫晧以為奉禁都尉，使其占侯。 晧政嚴酷，訓知其必敗而不敢言。 時錢唐湖開，或言天下當太平，青蓋入洛陽。 晧以問訓，訓曰：「臣止能望氣，不能達湖之開塞。 」退而告其友曰：「青蓋入洛，將有輿櫬銜璧之事，非吉祥也。 」尋而吳亡。 訓隨例內徙，拜諫義大夫。 俄而去職還鄉。
Chen Xun, courtesy name Daoyuan, came from Liyang. As a youth he devoured esoteric studies—astronomy, calendar math, yin-yang, and omen-reading—and excelled above all at wind-angle divination. The last Wu emperor Sun Hao named him palace attendant for forbidden precincts and set him to read the omens. Sun Hao ruled with terror; Chen Xun saw the dynasty was doomed but kept silent. When Qiantang Lake burst its banks, court gossip took it for an omen of universal peace and the Wu ruler's green-canopy carriage arriving in Luoyang. Sun Hao pressed him; Chen Xun answered carefully that he could read vapors, not hydraulics. Privately he warned a friend that "green canopy to Luoyang" foretold a funeral surrender, not fortune. Wu fell almost immediately afterward. He relocated with the other southern households and received the remonstrance grandee's title. He soon resigned and went home to Liyang.
3
及陳敏作亂，遣弟宏為曆陽太守，訓謂邑人曰：「陳家無王氣，不久當滅。 」宏聞，將斬之。 訓鄉人秦琚為宏參軍，乃說訓曰：「訓善風角，可試之。 如不中，徐斬未晚也。 」乃赦之。 時宏攻征東參軍衡彥于曆陽，乃問訓曰：「城中有幾千人？ 攻之可拔不？ 」訓登牛渚山望氣，曰：「不過五百人。 然不可攻，攻之必敗。 」宏復大怒曰：「何有五千人攻五百人而有不得理？ 」命將士攻之，果為彥所敗，方信訓有道術，乃優遇之。
When Chen Min rose and installed his brother Chen Hong at Liyang, Chen Xun told neighbors the Chen house carried no imperial aura and would collapse soon. Chen Hong planned to kill him for the remark. Army adviser Qin Ju, a townsman, begged Chen Hong to try Chen Xun's wind-angle art before shedding blood. If his reading failed, they could execute him at leisure. Chen Hong stayed the blade. While Chen Hong besieged Eastern Campaign aide Heng Yan in Liyang, he demanded to know the garrison's strength. He asked whether the walls could be stormed. Chen Xun climbed Mount Niuzhu, read the vapors, and put the defenders under five hundred. He forbade an assault anyway, warning that any attack would fail. Chen Hong fumed that five thousand ought to overrun five hundred. The storming host was routed by Heng Yan; chastened, Chen Hong honored Chen Xun as a true adept.
4
都水參軍淮南周亢嘗問訓以官位，訓曰：「君至卯年當剖符近郡，酉年當有曲蓋。 」亢曰：「脫如來言，當相薦拔。 」訓曰：「性不好官，惟欲得米耳。 」後亢果為義興太守、金紫將軍。 時劉聰、王彌寇洛陽，曆陽太守武瑕問訓曰：「國家人事如何？ 」訓曰：「胡賊三逼，國家當敗，天子野死。 今尚未也。 」其後懷湣二帝果有平陽之酷焉。 或問其以明年吉凶者，訓曰：「揚州刺史當死，武昌大火，上方節將亦當死。 」至時，劉陶、周訪皆卒，武昌大火，燒數千家。 時甘卓為曆陽太守，訓私謂所親曰：「甘侯頭低而視仰，相法名為眄刀，又目有赤脈，自外而入，不出十年，必以兵死，不領兵則可以免。 」卓果為王敦所害。 丞相王導多病，每自憂慮，以問訓。 訓曰：「公耳豎垂肩，必壽，亦大貴，子孫當興于江東。 」咸如其言。 訓年八十餘卒。
Zhou Kang of Huainan, an aide on waterworks, asked his career; Chen Xun promised a nearby governorship in a mao year and a bent-canopy general's train in a you year. Zhou Kang vowed to pull strings if the prophecy held. Chen Xun said he wanted grain, not promotion. Zhou Kang later became Yixing governor and a gold-and-purple general, just as foretold. When Liu Cong and Wang Mi threatened Luoyang, Liyang governor Wu Xia asked Chen Xun for the fate of the Jin house. Chen Xun said Xiongnu armies would thrice corner the throne, the dynasty would fall, and the emperor would perish in the field. The worst had not arrived yet. Emperors Huai and Min later endured captivity and murder at Pingyang, as he had warned. Asked about the coming year, he predicted the Yangzhou governor's death, a conflagration at Wuchang, and the passing of a senior commander. Liu Tao and Zhou Fang died on schedule, and Wuchang blazed through thousands of homes. Watching Gan Zhuo at Liyang, Chen Xun whispered that his low head and upturned eyes formed the lethal "knife-squint" look, laced with red veins—within a decade steel would find him unless he shed command. Gan Zhuo fell to Wang Dun's coup, sword in hand. Chancellor Wang Dao, chronically unwell, consulted Chen Xun in his anxiety. Chen Xun read his pendulous ears as signs of long life, high rank, and a flourishing lineage in Jiangdong. Each prediction proved true. He died past eighty.
5
戴洋
Dai Yang
6
戴洋，字國流，吳興長城人也。 年十二，遇病死，五日而蘇。 說死時天使其為酒藏吏，授符錄，給吏從幡麾，將上蓬萊、昆侖、積石、太室、恆、廬、衡等諸山。 既而遣歸，逢一老父，謂之曰：「汝後當得道，為貴人所識。 」及長，遂善風角。
Dai Yang, courtesy name Guoliu, was a native of Changcheng in Wuxing commandery. At twelve he sickened, "died," and woke again after five days. He described a posthumous posting as celestial cellar-keeper with registers, escorts, and a tour of the sacred peaks from Penglai to the great Heng ranges. Sent back to life, an elder promised he would win the Dao and earn patronage from the mighty. As an adult he mastered wind-angle divination.
7
為人短陋，無風望，然好道術，妙解占侯卜數。 吳末為台吏，知吳將亡，託病不仕。 及吳平，還鄉里。 後行至瀨鄉，經老子祠，皆是洋昔死時所見使處，但不復見昔物耳。 因問守藏應鳳曰：「去二十餘年，嘗有人乘馬東行，過老君而不下馬，未達橋，墜馬死者不？ 」鳳言有之。 所問之事，多與洋同。
He was homely and slight, yet obsessed with occult arts and uncannily sharp at omens, oracles, and fate reckoning. Late in Wu he held a clerkship at headquarters, saw the kingdom's end coming, and feigned illness to stay out of service. After the conquest of Wu he went home. Passing Laozi's shrine at Lai township, he recognized every corner from his otherworldly errand, though the spirit furnishings had vanished. He asked keeper Ying Feng whether a rider had once insulted the god by staying mounted and died before the bridge—twenty years past. Ying Feng confirmed the tale. Every detail matched Dai Yang's infernal itinerary.
8
揚州刺史嘗問吉凶於洋，答曰：「熒惑入南斗，八月有暴水，九月當有客軍西南來。 」如期果大水，而石冰作亂。 冰既據揚州，洋謂人曰：「視賊雲氣，四月當破。 」果如其言。 時陳敏為右將軍，堂邑令孫混見而羨之。 洋曰：「敏當作賊族滅，何足願也！ 」未幾，敏果反而誅焉。 初，混欲迎其家累，洋曰：「此地當敗，得臘不得正，豈可移家於賊中乎！ 」混便止。 歲末，敏弟昶攻堂邑，混遂以單身走免。 其後都水馬武舉洋為都水令史，洋請急還鄉。 將赴洛，夢神人謂之曰：「洛中當敗，人盡南渡，後五年揚州必有天子。 」洋信之，遂不去。 既而皆如其夢。
Consulted by the Yangzhou governor, he warned of Mars in the Dipper—cloudbursts in the eighth month and an alien column from the southwest in the ninth. The floods came on time, and Shi Bing's revolt followed. Once Shi Bing held Yangzhou, Dai Yang read his banners and gave him until the fourth month to collapse. The rebellion fell in that month. Chen Min, General of the Right, drew envious stares from Sun Hun, magistrate of Tangyi. Dai Yang snapped that Chen Min would turn traitor and wipe his own line—hardly a model to covet. Chen Min revolted and died under the blade almost at once. Sun Hun meant to fetch his kin; Dai Yang swore the town would fall after la but before the new year and forbade dragging families into a war zone. Sun Hun stayed put. When Chen Min's brother Chen Chang stormed Tangyi at year's end, Sun Hun slipped away alone. Ma Wu of the waterways directorate named him a waterways clerk; Dai Yang begged leave and hurried home. Bound for Luoyang, he dreamed a god warning of the capital's fall, a great southern flight, and an emperor in Yangzhou within five years. He canceled the journey and believed the vision. Events unfolded exactly as the dream had said.
9
廬江太守華譚問洋曰：「天下誰當復作賊者？ 」洋曰：「王機。 」尋而機反。 陳眕問洋曰：「人言江南當有貴人，顧彥先、周宣珮當是不？ 」洋曰：「顧不及臘，周不見來年八月。 」榮果以十二月十七日卒，十九日臘，珮以明年七月晦亡。 王導遇病，召洋問之。 洋曰：「君侯本命在申，金為土使之主，而于申上石頭立冶，火光照天，此為金火相爍，水火相煎，以故受害耳。 」導即移居東府，病遂差。
Lujiang governor Hua Tan asked who in the realm would next rise in rebellion. Dai Yang answered, "Wang Ji." Wang Ji revolted almost at once. Chen Zhen asked whether Gu Rong and Zhou Pei were the great men fate had marked for the south. Dai Yang said Gu Rong would not live to la and Zhou Pei would die before the eighth month of the coming year. Gu Rong died on the seventeenth of the twelfth month, la came two days later, and Zhou Pei perished on the final day of the seventh month next year—each on schedule. Wang Dao took sick and called Dai Yang to his bedside. He traced Wang Dao's fate to the shen stem, where a royal foundry atop Stone Citadel set metal and fire at war and poisoned the patron of earth. Wang Dao relocated to the Eastern Secretariat compound and recovered.
10
鎮東從事中郎張闓舉洋為丞相令史。 時司馬颺為烏程令，將赴職，洋曰：「君宜深慎下吏。 」揚後果坐吏免官。 洋又謂曰：「卿雖免官，十一月當作郡，加將軍。 」至期，為太山太守、鎮武將軍。 颺賣宅將行，洋止之曰：「君不得至，當還，不可無宅。 」颺果為徐龕所逼，不得之郡。 元帝增颺眾二千，使助祖逖。 洋勸颺不行，颺乃稱疾。 收付廷尉，俄而因赦得出。
Zhang Kai, staff officer to the general who guards the east, recommended him as a chancellery clerk. When Sima Yang left for his Wucheng magistracy, Dai Yang warned him to watch his underlings. Sima Yang was cashiered when a clerk's guilt touched him. Dai Yang added that in the eleventh month he would govern a commandery with a general's commission. On the date he was named Taishan governor and general who guards martial might. As Sima Yang sold his house to leave, Dai Yang told him he would never reach Taishan and must keep a roof in the capital. Xu Kan's revolt blocked his march and sent him home. Emperor Yuan bolstered Sima Yang with two thousand troops for Zu Ti's campaign. Dai Yang begged him not to march; Sima Yang pleaded sickness instead. The court jailed him briefly until an amnesty freed him.
11
元帝將登阼，使洋擇日，洋以為宜用三月二十四日丙午。 太史令陳卓奏用二十二日，言：「昔越王用甲辰三月反國，范蠡稱在陽之前，當主盡出，上下盡空，德將出遊，刑入中宮，今與此同。 」洋曰：「越王為吳所囚，雖當時遜媚，實懷怨憤，蠡故用甲辰，乘德而歸，留刑吳宮。 今大王內無含咎，外無怨憤，當承天洪命，納祚無窮，何為追越王去國留殃故事邪！ 」乃從之。
For Yuan-di's enthronement Dai Yang picked the bingwu day of the third month's twenty-fourth. Chen Zhuo countered with the twenty-second, citing Yue's jiachen return and Fan Li's doctrine of empty hosts and wandering virtue. Dai Yang replied that Goujian's calendar trick had humiliated a captor-king, not crowned a legitimate heir. Yuan-di, he argued, was blameless and free of grudge—he should accept an auspicious enthronement date, not Yue's vengeful omen. The throne accepted Dai Yang's day.
12
及祖約代兄鎮譙，請洋為中典軍，遷督護。 四月庚辰，禺中時有大風，起自東南，折木。 洋謂約曰：「十月必有賊到譙城東，至曆陽，南方有反者。 」主簿王振以洋為妖，白約收洋，付刺奸而絕其食五十日，言語如故。 約知其有神術，乃赦之而讓振。 振後有罪被收，洋救之。 約曰：「振往日相系，今何以救之？ 」洋曰：「振不識風角，非有宿嫌。 振往時垂餓死，洋養活之，振猶尚遺忘。 夫處富貴而不棄貧賤甚難。 」約義之，即原振，賜洋米三十石。 至十月三日，石勒騎果到譙城東。 洋言於約曰：「賊必向城父，可遣騎水南追之，步軍于水北斷要路，賊必敗。 」約竟不追，賊乃掠城父婦女輜重而去。 約將魯延求追賊，洋曰：「不可。 」約不從，使兄子智與延追之。 賊偽棄婦女輜重走，智與延等爭物，賊還掩之，智、延僅以身免，士卒皆死。 約表洋為下邑長。 時梁國人反，逐太守袁晏。 梁城峻險，約欲討之而未決，洋曰：「賊以八月辛酉日反，日辰俱王，辛德在南方，酉受自刑，梁在譙北，乘德伐刑，賊必破亡。 又甲子日東風而雷西行，譙在東南，雷在軍前，為軍驅除。 昔吳伐關羽，天雷在前，周瑜拜賀。 今與往同，故知必克。 」約從之，果平梁城。
When Zu Yue succeeded his brother on the Qiao front, he took Dai Yang as central-army adviser and raised him to superintendent. On a fourth-month gengchen day, midmorning brought a southeast gale that snapped trees. Dai Yang told Zu Yue that raiders would strike east of Qiao toward Liyang in the tenth month while the south also rose in revolt. Registrar Wang Zhen called it witchcraft and had him starved fifty days in the interrogation cells without breaking him. Zu Yue saw his power was real, freed him, and scolded Wang Zhen. When Wang Zhen later faced charges, Dai Yang interceded. Zu Yue asked why he would rescue a man who had chained him. Dai Yang said Wang Zhen had acted from ignorance, not malice. He reminded Zu Yue that he had once fed Wang Zhen when the clerk was starving—a debt Wang Zhen forgot. Few who sit in silk remember friends in rags. Moved, Zu Yue spared Wang Zhen and paid Dai Yang thirty shi of grain. On the third day of the tenth month, Shi Le's horsemen appeared east of Qiao, exactly as Dai Yang had said. Dai Yang urged Zu Yue: "They will strike for Chengfu—ride around the south bank to catch them, seal the fords on the north bank, and you will break them." Zu Yue refused to move; the raiders looted Chengfu's people and wagons and rode away unopposed. General Lu Yan begged leave to pursue, but Dai Yang said, "Do not send them." Zu Yue ignored the warning and dispatched his nephew Zu Zhi alongside Lu Yan. The enemy dropped camp followers and supply carts as bait; Zu Zhi and Lu Yan fell to looting, whereupon the riders doubled back and cut them to pieces. The two commanders fled alone; every trooper perished. Zu Yue had him appointed magistrate of Xiayi in recognition of his counsel. The people of Liang commandery rose up and expelled their governor, Yuan Yan. Liang's walls were formidable and Zu Yue hesitated. Dai Yang read the stems: "They rose on xinyou in the eighth month when day and hour both read 'ruler'; xin's power lies south while the you branch turns on itself—Liang sits north of Qiao, so your host rides ascendant virtue against a self-consuming sign and the rebels cannot endure." Moreover, on a jiazi day an east wind carried thunder westward; Qiao lies southeast of that path, so the peal clears the road ahead of your host. When Wu struck Guan Yu, lightning heralded the advance, and Zhou Yu hailed it as a good omen. The signs match that campaign—we will take Liang." Zu Yue listened and reduced Liang as predicted.
13
正月，有大流星東南行，洋曰：「至秋，府當移壽陽。 」及王敦作逆，約問其勝敗，洋曰：「太白在東方，辰星不出。 兵法先起為主，應者為客。 辰星若出，太白為主，辰星為客。 辰星不出，太白為客，先起兵者敗。 今有客無主，有前無後，宜傳檄所部，應詔伐之。 」約乃率眾向合肥。 俄而敦死眾敗，遂住壽陽。 洋又曰：「江淮之間當有軍事，譙城虛曠，宜還固守。 不者，雍丘、沛皆非官有也。 」約不從，豫土遂陷於賊。
A great meteor streaked southeast in the first month; Dai Yang said, "Before autumn your command post will move to Shouyang." When Wang Dun turned traitor, Zu Yue asked the outcome. Dai Yang replied, "Venus hangs in the east and Mercury stays hidden. By the art of war the first mover is 'host' and the responder is 'guest.' If Mercury rises, Venus counts as host and Mercury as guest. With Mercury still absent, Venus plays guest: the side that strikes first loses." Today you have a foe without a champion in the field—no depth behind the vanguard. Issue orders up and down the army and march under edict to crush him." Zu Yue marched his army toward Hefei. Wang Dun soon died and his forces scattered; Zu Yue ended up stationed at Shouyang. Dai Yang added, "Trouble is brewing between the Yangzi and the Huai. Qiao lies empty—you should fall back and fortify it. Otherwise you will lose Yongqiu and Pei alike to the enemy." Zu Yue ignored him, and the Central Plain south of the Yellow River slipped into rebel hands.
14
春，約南行佃，遇大雷雨西南來，洋曰：「甲子西南天雷，其夏必失大將。 」至夏，汝南人反，執約兄子濟，送于石勒。 約府內地忽赤如丹，洋曰：「案《河圖徵》云：『地赤如丹血丸丸，當有下反上者。 』恐十月二十七日胡馬當來飲淮水。 」至時，石勒騎大至，攻城大戰。 其日西風，兵火俱發，約大懼。 會風回，賊退。 時傳言勒遣騎向壽陽，約欲送其家還江東，洋曰：「必無此事。 」尋而傳言果妄。
That spring Zu Yue rode south to oversee the harvest and met a thunderstorm out of the southwest. Dai Yang warned, "Thunder from the southwest on a jiazi day means you will lose a major general that summer." That summer Runan rose in revolt, captured Zu Yue's nephew Zu Ji, and handed him to Shi Le. The soil inside Zu Yue's compound flushed red as lacquer. Dai Yang cited the River Chart augury: "When the ground turns cinnabar-red like clots of blood, inferiors will revolt against superiors." I dread the twenty-seventh of the tenth month, when barbarian horses will drink from the Huai." On that day Shi Le's cavalry closed in and a fierce siege battle erupted. A gale blew from the west; fire and arms flared together, and Zu Yue was terrified. Then the wind swung round and the attackers drew off. Rumors claimed Shi Le was riding on Shouyang; Zu Yue prepared to evacuate his family to the southland. Dai Yang said the report was false. The scare proved baseless.
15
咸和初，月暈左角，有赤白珥。 約問洋，洋曰：「角為天門，開布陽道，官門當有大戰。 」俄而蘇峻遣使招約俱反，洋謂約曰：「蘇峻必敗，然其初起，兵鋒不可當，可外和內嚴，以待其變。 」約不從，遂與峻反。 至三年五月，大風雷雨西北來，城內晦螟，洋謂約曰：「雷鳴人上，明使君當遠佞近直，愛下振貧。 昔秦有此變，卒致亂亡。 」約大怒，收洋系之。 遣部將李概將兵到盧江，其眾盡散。 約召洋出，問之曰：「吾還東何如留壽陽？ 若留壽陽，何如入胡？ 」洋曰：「東入失半，入胡滅門，留壽陽尚可。 」約欲東向曆陽，其眾不樂東下，皆叛約，劫約姊及嫂奔于石勒。 約到曆陽，祖煥問洋曰：「君昔言平西在壽陽可得五年，果如君言。 今在曆陽，可得幾時？ 」洋曰：「得六月耳。 」約問洋：「台下及此氣侯何如？ 」洋曰：「此當復有反者。 台下來年三月當太平，江州當大喪。 後南方復有軍事，去此千里。 」尋而牽騰叛約，約率所親將家屬奔于石勒。 二月而天子反正，四月而溫嶠卒，郭默據湓口以叛。 後勒誅約及親屬並盡，皆如洋言。
Early in Xianhe, a lunar halo ringed the moon's left horn with crimson and white 'ears.' Zu Yue asked the meaning. Dai Yang said, "The horn is the Gate of Heaven; when it opens the yang road, bloodshed reaches the palace." Soon Su Jun invited Zu Yue into his revolt. Dai Yang warned, "Su Jun is doomed, but his first rush will be unstoppable—feign accord while tightening your guard and wait for his tide to turn." Zu Yue refused the advice and cast his lot with Su Jun. In the fifth month of the third Xianhe year a northwest storm plunged the city into gloom. Dai Yang told Zu Yue, "Thunder over the people means the governor must banish sycophants, embrace honest men, care for the ranks, and succor the destitute. Qin saw the same sign and fell to ruin." Zu Yue flew into a rage and had Dai Yang thrown in chains. He dispatched Li Gai toward Lujiang, but the column melted away. Zu Yue released Dai Yang and asked whether to retreat east or stay in Shouyang. If he stayed, should he next throw in with the barbarians?" Dai Yang answered, "Flight east costs you half your following; submission to the Hu wipes out your house; holding Shouyang is the least ill choice." Zu Yue tried to march for Liyang, but his troops refused to go east, mutinied, and carried his sister and sister-in-law off to Shi Le. At Liyang, Zu Huan reminded Dai Yang, "You said the 'Pacifier of the West' could keep Shouyang five years, and you were right. Now that he is here in Liyang, how long does he have?" Dai Yang said, "Six months, no more." Zu Yue pressed him about omens at court and in the field. Dai Yang replied, "Another revolt stirs here. The capital will quiet down by the third month of next year, but Jiangzhou will suffer a great bereavement. Later still, fighting will flare a thousand li to the south." Soon Qian Teng turned on Zu Yue; Zu fled with kinsmen and clients to Shi Le. The second month saw the emperor restored; in the fourth month Wen Jiao died, and Guo Mo seized Penkou in revolt. Shi Le later executed Zu Yue and wiped out his entire clan—just as Dai Yang had foretold.
16
約既敗，洋往尋陽。 時劉胤鎮尋陽，胤問洋曰：「我病當差不？ 」洋曰：「不憂使君不差，憂使君今年有大厄。 使君年四十七，行年入庚寅。 《太公陰謀》曰：『六庚為白獸，在上為客星，在下為害氣。 』年與命並，必凶當忌。 十二月二十二日庚寅勿見客。 」胤曰：「我當解職，將君還野中治病。 」洋曰：「使君當作江州，不得解職。 」胤曰：「溫公不復還邪？ 」洋曰：「溫公雖還，使君故作江州。 」俄如其言。 九月甲寅申時，回風從東來，入胤兒船中，西過，狀如匹練，長五六丈。 洋曰：「風從咸池下來，攝提下去，咸池為刀兵，大殺為死喪。 到甲子日申時，府內大聚骨理之。 胤問在何處，洋曰：「不出州府門也。 」胤架府東門。 洋又曰：「東為天牢，牢下開門，憂天獄至。 」十二月十七日，洋又曰：「臘近可閉門，以五十人備守，並以百人備東北寅上，以卻害氣。 」胤不從。 二十四日壬辰，胤遂為郭默所害。
When Zu Yue fell, Dai Yang made his way to Xunyang. Liu Yin, who held Xunyang, asked whether he would recover from his illness. Dai Yang said, "Your sickness is not what troubles me; this year brings you a far worse stroke of fate. You are forty-seven, and your annual star has entered gengyin. The Taigong yinmou says, "The six geng days are the White Beast—above they mark the guest star, below they unleash baleful qi." When the year-pillar matches your nativity, disaster follows unless you ward it off. On the twenty-second of the twelfth month, a gengyin day, admit no visitors." Liu Yin said, "I will resign and retire with you to the countryside to heal." Dai Yang answered, "You are fated to govern Jiangzhou—you cannot step down." Liu Yin asked, "Will Minister Wen not come back from the capital?" Dai Yang said, "Even when Wen returns, you will still take Jiangzhou." Events unfolded exactly as he predicted. On a jiayin day in the ninth month, around midafternoon, a whirlwind blew from the east into Liu Yin's son's boat, then swept westward like a five- or six-zhang ribbon of cloth. Dai Yang said, "That wind dropped from the Xianchi asterism while Sheti sank below—Xianchi presages arms, and 'great killing' means death. On the next jiazi day at the shen hour your staff will gather a great heap of bones for burial." Liu Yin asked where; Dai Yang said, "Within the walls of your command—not beyond the gate." Liu Yin had scaffolding raised at the east gate of his compound. Dai Yang added, "East is the Celestial Prison; opening a gate under it invites heaven's dungeon to close on you." On the seventeenth of the twelfth month he warned again: "Seal the gates for the year-end rites—fifty guards on the doors and a hundred men on the northeast yin corner to turn the baleful qi." Liu Yin ignored him. On the twenty-fourth, a renchen day, Guo Mo murdered Liu Yin.
17
南中郎將桓宣以洋為參軍，將隨宣往襄陽，太尉陶侃留之住武昌。 時侃謀北伐，洋曰：「前年十一月熒惑守胃昴，至今年四月，積五百餘日。 昴，趙之分野，石勒遂死。 熒惑以七月退，從畢右順行入黃道，未及天關，以八月二十二日復逆行還鉤，繞畢向昴。 昴畢為邊兵，主胡夷，故置天弓以射之。 熒惑逆行，司無德之國，石勒死是也。 勒之餘燼，以自殘害。 今年官與太歲、太陰三合癸巳，癸為北方，北方當受災。 歲鎮二星共合翼軫，從子及巳，徘徊六年。 荊楚之分，歲鎮所守，其下國昌，豈非功德之徵也！ 今年六月，鎮星前角亢。 角亢，鄭之分。 歲星移入房，太白在心。 心房，宋分。 順之者昌，逆之者亡。 石季龍若興兵東南，此其死會也。 官若應天伐刑，徑據宋鄭，則無敵矣。 若天與不取，反受其咎。 」侃志在中原，聞而大喜。 會病篤，不果行。
General Huan Xuan took Dai Yang as adjutant for a march to Xiangyang, but Grand Commandant Tao Kan kept him at Wuchang instead. Tao Kan was planning a northern strike. Dai Yang said, "Mars lingered in the Pleiades and Hyades from the eleventh month of before last until the fourth month of this year—more than five hundred days. Those lodges mark the Zhao sector; Shi Le died under that sign. Mars went direct in the seventh month, sliding east along the ecliptic from the Net; before it reached the Celestial Gate it turned retrograde on the twenty-second of the eighth, looped through the Hook, skirted the Net, and bore down on the Pleiades again. The Net and Pleiades govern border hosts and northern tribes—heaven strings the Bow to shoot them down. Retrograde Mars punishes a realm without virtue; Shi Le's end fits the pattern. The sparks of his house will consume one another. This year the bureaucracy star, Jupiter, and Saturn meet in guisi; gui points north—calamity will strike the northern heartland. Jupiter and Saturn share the lodges Yi and Zhen from zi through si, hovering there six years. Those stars watch the Jing-Chu sector—where they stand long, the state below flourishes. Surely that marks your merit!" This sixth month Saturn advances before Horn and Gullet. Horn and Gullet are the Zheng heartland. Jupiter enters Room while Venus sits in Heart. Heart and Room mark the Song sector. Follow heaven's pointer and you prosper; defy it and you perish. If Shi Hu marches southeast, he walks into his own death day. If the court rides those signs to punish evil and seizes Song and Zheng, no enemy will withstand you. Heaven offers the chance—refuse it and you invite disaster on yourself. Tao Kan's heart was set on the north; the reading delighted him. He fell mortally ill and never marched.
18
侃薨，征西將軍庾亮代鎮武昌，復引洋問氣侯。 洋曰：「天有白氣，喪必東行，不過數年必應。 」尋有大鹿向西城門，洋曰：「野獸向城，主人將去。 」城東家夜半望見城內有數炬火，從城上出，如大車狀，白布幔覆，與火俱出城東北行，至江乃滅。 洋聞而歎曰：「此與前白氣同。 」時亮欲西鎮石城，或問洋：「此西足當欲東不？ 」洋曰：「不當也。 」，洋言於亮曰：「武昌土地有山無林，政可圖始，不可居終。 山作八字，數不及九。 昔吳用壬寅來上； 創立宮城，至己酉，還下秣陵。 陶公亦涉八年。 土地盛衰有數，人心去就有期，不可移也。 公宜更擇吉處，武昌不可久住。 」五年，亮令毛寶屯邾城。 九月，洋言於亮曰：「毛豫州今年受死問。 昨朝大霧晏風，當有怨賊報仇，攻圍諸侯，誠宜遠偵邏。 」寶問當在何時，答曰：「五十日內。 」其夕，又曰：「九月建戌，硃雀飛驚，征軍還歸，乘戴火光，天示有信，災發東房，葉落歸本，慮有後患。 」明日，又曰：「昨夜火殃，非國福，今年架屋，致使君病，可因燒屋，移家南渡，無嫌也。 」寶即遣兒婦還武昌。 尋傳賊當來攻城，洋曰：「十月丁亥夜半時得賊問，幹為君，支為臣，丁為征西府，亥為邾城，功曹為賊神，加子時十月水王木相，王相氣合，賊必來。 寅數七，子數九，賊高可九千人，下可七千人。 從魁為貴人加丁，下克上，有空亡之事，不敢進武昌也。 」賊果陷邾城而去。 亮問洋曰：「故當不失石城否？ 」洋曰：「賊從安陸向石城，逆太白，當伐身，無所慮。 」亮曰：「天何以利胡而病我？ 」洋曰：「天符有吉凶，土地有盛衰，今年害氣三合己亥，己為天下，亥為戎胡，季龍亦當受死。 今乃不憂賊，但憂公病耳。 」亮曰：「何方救我疾？ 」洋曰：「荊州受兵，江州受災，公可去此二州。 」亮曰：「如此，當有解不」？ 」洋曰：「恨晚，猶差不也。 」亮竟不能解二州，遂至大困。 洋曰：「昔蘇峻時，公于白石祠中祈福，許賽其牛，至今未解，故為此鬼所考。 」亮曰：「有之，君是神人也。 」或問洋曰：「庾公可得幾時？ 」洋曰：「見明年。 」時亮已不識人，咸以為妄，果至正月一日而薨。
After Tao Kan died, Yu Liang succeeded him at Wuchang and again consulted Dai Yang on the omens. Dai Yang said, "A white vapor spans the sky—bereavement is traveling east and will show itself within a few years." Soon afterward a huge deer walked toward the west gate. Dai Yang said, "Beasts turning on the walls mean the lord will leave." That night townsfolk east of the wall saw balls of flame lift from the battlements like covered wagons swathed in white; they drifted northeast out of the city, reached the river, and vanished. Dai Yang heard the tale and murmured, "That is the same white vapor I warned about." Yu Liang meant to shift his seat west to Stone City; someone asked Dai Yang whether that would check an eastward push. Dai Yang said, "No—that will not answer the threat." He then told Yu Liang, "Wuchang is ridged and bare of woodland: fine for founding a foothold, fatal as a long-term capital." The hills trace the form of the graph for "eight," and the numerology never reaches nine—a place that cannot endure. Eastern Wu once chose a renyin year to move upstream; they raised the palace there, yet by jiyou they had retreated again to Moling below. Tao Kan too held the place only eight years. Soil has its seasons of fortune, and popular allegiance its term—no edict can fix what heaven has timed. You must pick a luckier seat; Wuchang will not hold you long." In the fifth year Yu Liang posted Mao Bao to garrison Zhucheng. That ninth month Dai Yang warned Yu Liang, "Your prefect Mao Bao carries a death omen this year." Heavy fog and a tardy wind mean vengeful raiders will ring a border town—double your patrols." Mao Bao asked the timing; Dai Yang answered, "Inside fifty days." That night he added arcana about the xu month, the Vermilion Bird, and fire omens—warning that ruin would strike the eastern wing and leave lasting trouble. Next morning he said the overnight blaze boded ill for the realm, blamed recent roofing for Yu Liang's illness, and urged burning the new halls and moving the household south. Mao Bao sent his daughter-in-law back to Wuchang at once. When word spread of a siege, Dai Yang cast the stems: at midnight on dinghai in the tenth month the divination showed the enemy would appear, with strengths between seven and nine thousand. The oracle reckoned their strength at seven to nine thousand men. Other lines showed "emptiness"—they would not dare strike Wuchang itself. The raiders did seize Zhucheng, then withdrew. Yu Liang asked whether Stone City would still hold. Dai Yang said their march from Anlu toward Stone City ran counter to Venus—they would hurt themselves; the rock fort was safe. Yu Liang cried, "Why does Heaven bless the barbarians and scourge us?" Dai Yang answered that heaven's signs cut both ways—this year baleful stars joined at jihai, marking the barbarians and predicting Shi Hu's death as well. Forget the enemy, he said; worry instead about Yu Liang's own sickness." Yu Liang asked where to seek a cure. Dai Yang told him to quit both Jingzhou and Jiangzhou—the stars marked them for war and plague. Yu Liang asked, "Is there still a way out?" Dai Yang said, "Very late—but partial relief remains possible." Yu Liang could not abandon either command and sank into crisis. Dai Yang explained an unpaid vow—a promised ox at Baishi shrine during Su Jun's rebellion—that a lingering spirit now collected. Yu Liang admitted the vow and called him a seer. Someone asked how long Yu Liang would live. Dai Yang said, "Only into next year." By then Yu Liang was beyond speech; courtiers mocked the prophecy—yet he died on New Year's Day.
19
庾翼代亮，洋復為占侯。 少時卒，年八十餘。 所占驗者不可勝紀。
Yu Yi succeeded his brother, and Dai Yang continued casting omens for him. Dai Yang died in his eighties not long after. His verified predictions are too many to list.
20
韓友
Han You
21
韓友，字景先，廬江舒人也。 為書生，受《易》于會稽伍振，善占卜，能圖宅相塚，亦行京費厭勝之術。 龍舒長鄧林婦病積年，垂死，醫巫皆息意。 友為筮之，使畫作野豬著臥處屏風上，一宿覺佳，於是遂差。 舒縣廷掾王睦病死，已復魄。 友為筮之，令以丹畫版作日月置床頭，又以豹皮馬鄣泥臥上，立愈。 劉世則女病魅積年，巫為攻禱，伐空塚故城間，得狸鼉數十，病猶不差。 友筮之，命作布囊，依女發時，張囊著窗牖間，友閉戶作氣，若有所驅。 斯須之間，見囊大脹如吹，因決敗之，女仍大發。 友乃更作皮囊二枚，遝張之，施張如前，囊復脹滿。 因急縛囊口，懸著樹二十許日，漸消，開視有二斤狐毛，女遂差。
Han You, courtesy name Jingxian, came from Shu county in Lujiang commandery. He studied the Zhouyi under Wu Zhen of Kuaiji, excelled at yarrow divination, geomancy of houses and graves, and the apotropaic methods of Jing Fang and Fei Zhi. Deng Lin, magistrate of Longshu, had a wife dying of a chronic malady after healers and exorcists had abandoned hope. Han You cast the yarrow and told them to paint a boar on her bedside screen; overnight she rallied and then mended. Wang Mu, a county clerk, had died and then returned to life. Han You prescribed cinnabar sun-and-moon tablets at the pillow, leopard skin, a horse curtain, and clay on the couch—cures that worked at once. Liu Shize's daughter suffered a long haunting; exorcists razed empty graves and dug up scores of badgers and turtles without curing her. Han You had a linen sack hung in the window when her fits began, then shut the door and performed a breath ritual as though expelling a thing. The sack suddenly ballooned; they ripped it open, and the girl convulsed worse than ever. He made two leather bags, layered them as before, and again they bulged tight. He lashed the mouths shut and hung them in a tree for twenty days until they deflated, revealing two jin of fox fur inside—after which the girl healed.
22
宣城邊洪以四月中就友卜家中安否，友曰：「卿家有兵殃，其禍甚重。 可伐七十束柴，積於庚地，至七月丁酉放火燒之，咎可消也。 不爾，其凶難言。 」洪即聚柴。 至日，大風，不敢發火。 洪後為廣陽領校，遭母喪歸家，友來投之，時日已暮，出告從者，速裝束，吾當夜去。 從者曰：「今日已暝，數十里草行，何急復去？ 」友曰：「非汝所知也。 此間血覆地，寧可復住！ 」苦留之，不待食而去。 其夜洪欻發狂，絞殺兩子，並殺婦，又斫父妾二人，皆被創，因出亡走。 明日，其宗族往收殯亡者，尋索洪，數日，于宅前林中得之，已自經死。
Bian Hong of Xuancheng asked Han You about domestic safety; the diviner warned of violent disaster looming over the house. He told him to stack seventy faggots on geng soil and burn them on dingyou in the seventh month to lift the curse." If he refused, Han You said, the harm would be beyond words." Bian Hong collected the wood. On the appointed day a gale rose and he dared not light the pyre. Later, as Bian Hong mourned his mother at home, Han You visited, then suddenly ordered his escort to saddle up for a midnight flight. His men protested that night had fallen and the road was long. Han You said they could not understand what he saw. "Blood will soak this yard," he said; "we cannot stay." Hosts pressed him to stay, but he rode off unfed. That night Bian Hong ran amok, throttled two sons, murdered his wife, wounded two concubines, and bolted. Next day kinsmen came to bury the dead and found Bian Hong hanged in the grove before his gate.
23
宣城太守殷祐有病，友筮之，曰：「七月晦日，將有大鸜鳥來集廳事上，宜勤伺取，若獲者為善，不獲將成禍。 」祐乃謹為其備。 至日，果有大鸜垂尾九尺，來集廳事上，掩捕得之，祐乃遷石頭督護，後為吳郡太守。
Governor Yin You of Xuancheng fell ill; Han You foretold a giant guisu bird on the hall on the seventh month's last day and urged him to capture it or suffer woe. Yin You made every preparation. The bird appeared as foretold; they seized it, and Yin You rose to Stone Rampart protector and later governor of Wu.
24
友卜占神效甚多，而消殃轉禍，無不皆驗。 于寶問其故，友曰：「筮封用五行相生殺，如案方投藥治病，以冷熱相救。 其差與不差，不可必也。 」友以舉賢良，元帝渡江，以為廣武將軍，永嘉末卒。
Han You's divinations were uncannily accurate, and his rites to turn away calamity never failed. Yu Bao asked how it worked; Han You compared yarrow work to prescribing medicine by pattern—warming or cooling the patient according to need. Whether the patient mends, he added, can never be guaranteed." Recommended as worthy, he became General Who Extends Martiality after the court crossed the river, and died late in Yongjia.
25
淳于智
Chunyu Zhi
26
淳于智，字叔平，濟北盧人也。 有思義，能《易》筮，善厭勝之術。 高平劉柔夜臥，鼠齧其左手中指，以問智。 智曰：「是欲殺君而不能，當為君使其反死。 」乃以硃書手腕橫文後三寸作田字，辟方一寸二分，使露手以臥。 明旦，有大鼠伏死手前。 譙人夏侯藻母病困，詣智卜，忽有一狐當門向之嗥。 藻怖愕，馳見智。 智曰：「其禍甚急，君速歸，在狐嗥處拊心啼哭，令家人驚怪，大小必出，一人不出，哭勿止，然後其禍可救也。 」藻還，如其言，母亦扶病而出。 家人既集，堂屋五間拉然而崩。 護軍張劭母病篤，智筮之，使西出市沐猴，系母臂，令傍人捶拍，恆使作聲，三日放去。 劭從之。 其猴出門即為犬所咋死，母病遂差。 上党鮑瑗家多喪病貧苦，或謂之曰：「淳于叔平神人也，君何不試就卜，知禍所在？ 」瑗性質直，不信卜筮，曰：「人生有命，豈卜筮所移！ 」會智來，應詹謂曰：「此君寒士，每多屯虞，君有通靈之思，可為一卦。 」智乃為卦，卦成，謂瑗曰：「君安宅失宜，故令君困。 君舍東北有大桑樹，君徑至市，入門數十步，當有一人持荊馬鞭者，便就買以懸此樹，三年當暴得財。 」瑗承言詣市，果得馬鞭，懸之三年，浚井，得錢數十萬，銅鐵器復二十餘萬，於是致贍，疾者亦愈。 其消災轉禍，不可勝紀，而卜筮所占，千百皆中。 應詹少亦多病，智乃為符使詹佩之，誦其文，既而皆驗，莫能學也。
Chunyu Zhi, courtesy name Shuping, was a native of Lu in Jibei commandery. He was principled, divined with the Zhouyi, and mastered apotropaic rites. Liu Rou of Gaoping awoke to find a rat had chewed his left middle finger and consulted Chunyu Zhi. Chunyu Zhi said the beast meant murder but lacked power—and he would turn the death back on the rat. He painted a vermilion "field" glyph on the wrist crease and bade Liu sleep with the hand uncovered. At dawn a large rat lay dead before that hand. Xia Hou Zao of Qiao sought a reading for his dying mother; a fox stood howling across his gateway. Terrified, Zao raced to Chunyu Zhi. Chunyu Zhi told him to rush home, wail beneath the fox until every member of the household ran outdoors—if one stayed inside, keep crying—and thus avert the blow. Zao did so, and even his ailing mother stumbled out. Once they were all outside, the five-bay hall crashed down. Protector Zhang Shao's mother lay dying; Chunyu Zhi sent him west to buy a macaque, bind it on her arm, keep it squealing under patting for three days, then release it. Zhang Shao obeyed. The monkey was killed by dogs at the door; the mother recovered. Bao Yuan of Shangdang suffered repeated deaths, sickness, and poverty; neighbors urged him to consult the "spirit man" Chunyu Zhi. Bao Yuan, blunt and skeptical, said fate ruled life—not yarrow. When Chunyu Zhi arrived, Ying Zhan begged a reading for the hard-pressed scholar. Chunyu Zhi cast the lines and said Bao Yuan's house sat on ill-oriented ground that beggared him. He told him to buy a thorn switch in the market and hang it on a great mulberry northeast of the house to draw sudden fortune within three years. Bao Yuan obeyed, found the whip, hung it, and three years later dredged tens of thousands of cash and bronze from his well—ending want and sickness in the household. His turnings of ill luck are beyond counting, and every yarrow reading struck true. Ying Zhan had been sickly in youth until Chunyu Zhi gave him talismans to wear and chant—cures that worked but could not be taught.
27
性深沈，常自言短命，曰：「辛亥歲天下有事，當有巫醫挾道術者死。 吾守《易》義以行之，猶當不應此乎！ 」太康末，為司馬督，有寵于楊駿，故見殺。
Brooding and self-aware, he predicted a xinhai-year purge that would kill occult healers. "I live by the Changes," he said, "yet even I cannot escape that fate!" Late in Taikang he served as marshal under Yang Jun's patronage and was executed in the coup.
28
步熊
Bu Xiong
29
步熊，字叔羆，陽平發幹人也。 少好卜筮數術，門徒甚盛。 熊學舍側有一人燒死，吏持熊諸生，謂為失火。 熊曰：「已為卿卜得其人矣。 使從道南行，當有一人來問得火主未者，便縛之。 」吏如熊言，果是耕人，自言草惡難耕，故燒之，忽風起延燒遠近，實不知草中有人。 又鄰人兒遠行，或告已死，其父母號哭制服，熊為之卜，克日當還，如期果至。 趙王倫聞其名，召之。 熊謂諸生曰：「倫死不久，不足應也。 」倫怒，遣兵圍之數重。 熊乃使諸生著其裘南走，倫兵悉赴捉之，熊密從北出，得脫。 後為成都王穎所辟，穎使熊射覆，物無所失。 後穎奔關中，平昌公模鎮鄴，以熊穎黨，誅之。
Bu Xiong, courtesy name Shupi, came from Fagan in Yangping commandery. From youth he loved yarrow and number lore and gathered many pupils. When a man burned to death beside his school, the magistrate seized Bu Xiong's disciples as arsonists. Bu Xiong said he had already identified the culprit by divination. He told the clerk to walk south until someone asked about the "fire's master," then seize him. The man was a farmer who had torched stubble for clearing; a gust spread the blaze and he never knew someone lay hidden in the weeds. When neighbors thought a boy dead abroad, Bu Xiong set a return date—and the youth walked home on that very day. Prince Sima Lun of Zhao summoned him to court. Bu Xiong told his pupils Sima Lun was doomed and the summons was beneath their notice. Sima Lun ringed the school with soldiers. He dressed disciples in his own robes as decoys while he slipped out the north side. Sima Ying of Chengdu employed him for "cover-shoot" divination, and he never failed to name the hidden object. When Sima Ying fled to Guanzhong and Sima Mo held Ye, Mo executed Bu Xiong as a partisan of the prince.
30
杜不愆
Du Buqian
31
杜不愆，廬江人也。 少就外祖郭璞學《易》卜。 屢有驗。 高平郗超年二十餘，得重疾，試令筮之。 不愆曰：「案卦言之，卿所苦尋除。 然宜於東北三十里上宮姓家索其所養雄雉，籠盛置東簷下，卻後九日丙午日午時，必當有雌雉飛來與交，既而雙去。 若如此，不出二十日病都除，又是休應，年將八十，位極人臣。 若但雌逝雄留者，病一周方差，年半八十，名位亦失。 」超時正羸篤，慮命在旦夕，笑而答曰：「若保八十之半，便有餘矣。 一周病差，何足為淹！ 」然未之信。 或勸依其言，索雉果得。 至丙午日，超臥南軒之下觀之，至日晏，果有雌雉飛入籠，與雄雉交而去，雄雉不動。 超歎曰：「雖管郭之奇，何以尚此！ 」超病彌年乃起，至四十，卒于中書郎。 不愆後占筮轉疏，無復此類。 後為桓嗣建威參軍。
Du Buqian came from Lujiang commandery. As a boy he learned the Zhouyi and yarrow lore under his grandfather Guo Pu. His readings proved true again and again. Xi Chao of Gaoping, barely twenty, fell dangerously ill; his household asked Du Buqian to cast. Du Buqian said the lines showed the ailment lifting soon. He prescribed a ritual: fetch a rooster from a Shang family on a rise thirty li northeast, cage it under the east eaves, and on the ninth day at noon a hen would arrive to mate— if that happened, the sickness would vanish within twenty days, he would live toward eighty, and rise to the highest ministerial rank. If the hen left while the cock stayed, he would mend after a week but lose half his years and his career prospects. Xi Chao, wasted and near death, laughed that half of eighty would be plenty. A week's convalescence seemed a trifle. Still he doubted the oracle. Friends pressed him to obey; he found the birds as directed. At noon on bingwu he watched from the south loggia until a hen flew in, coupled, and flew off while the rooster stayed. Xi Chao marveled that even Guan Lu and Guo Pu could not match such precision. His illness lingered a year before he rose; he died at forty as a secretary at the palace bureau. Later Du Buqian's casts grew rougher, and nothing so striking happened again. He ended as staff officer to Huan Si, general who establishes might.
32
嚴卿
Yan Qing
33
嚴卿，會稽人也。 善卜筮。 鄉人魏序欲暫東行，荒年多抄盜，令卿筮之。 卿筮曰：「君慎不可東行，必遭暴害之氣，而非劫也。 」序不之信。 卿曰：「既必不停，宜以禳之，可索西郭外獨母家白雄狗系著船前。 」求索止得駁狗，無白者。 卿曰：「駁者亦足，然猶恨其色不純，當餘小毒，正及六畜輩耳，無所復憂。 」序行半路，狗忽然作聲甚急，有如人打之者。 比視，已死，吐黑血鬥餘。 其夕，序墅上白鵝數頭無故自死，而序家無恙。
Yan Qing was a native of Kuaiji. He excelled at yarrow divination. Wei Xu of his village planned an eastern journey in a year of famine and robbers, and asked Yan Qing to cast. Yan Qing warned him not to travel east: violent qi awaited him, though not common bandits. Wei Xu ignored the warning. Yan Qing said if he insisted, he must tie a white rooster from a widow west of the wall to the bow as a ward. They could only find a spotted dog, no pure white fowl. Yan Qing said piebald would serve but hinted at leftover venom limited to livestock. Mid-voyage the dog yelped as if flogged. They found it dead, having spewed more than a dou of black blood. That night his white geese dropped dead, yet every human under his roof was spared.
34
隗炤
Wei Zhao
35
隗炤，汝陰人也。 善於《易》。 臨終，書版授其妻曰：「吾亡後當大荒窮，雖爾慎莫賣宅也。 卻後五年春，當有詔使來頓此亭，姓龔，此人負吾金，即以此版往責之，勿違言也。 」炤亡後，其家大困乏，欲賣宅，憶夫言輒止。 期日，有龔使者止亭中，妻遂齎版往責之。 使者執版惘然，不知所以。 妻曰：「夫臨亡，手書版見命如此，不敢妄也。 」使者沈吟良久而悟，謂曰：「賢夫何善？ 」妻曰：「夫善於《易》，而未會為人卜也。 」使者曰：「噫，可知矣！ 」乃命取蓍筮之，卦成，撫掌而歎曰：「妙哉隗生！ 含明隱跡，可謂鏡窮達而洞吉凶者也。 」於是告炤妻曰：「吾不相負金也，賢夫自有金耳，知亡後當暫窮，故藏金以待太平，所以不告兒婦者，恐金盡而困無已也。 知吾善《易》，故書版以寄意耳。 金有五百斤，盛以青甕，覆以銅柈，埋在堂屋東頭，去壁一丈，入地九尺。 」妻還掘之，皆如卜焉。
Wei Zhao came from Ruyin. He was a master of the Zhouyi. Dying, he gave his wife a wooden slip: after his death famine would strike, yet she must never sell the house. In five years a courier surnamed Gong would lodge at their post owing him gold—she must present the slip to collect. When want tempted her to sell, she remembered his charge and held the property. On the day foretold a Mr. Gong arrived; she brought him the tally for the debt. The messenger stared at the slip, baffled. She explained her husband's dying instructions. After long thought he asked what arts Wei Zhao had practiced. She said he knew the Zhouyi but never read for clients. The envoy exclaimed that he now understood. He cast the yarrow himself, then cried out in admiration for Wei Zhao's craft. He praised Wei for hiding brilliance while reading rise and fall with perfect clarity. He explained Wei had buried five hundred jin of gold for the lean years, telling no kin lest they spend it and starve. Wei knew the envoy understood the Changes, so he used the slip as cipher. He directed her to green jars under bronze lids, one zhang from the east wall and nine chi down. She dug and found every coin exactly as foretold.
36
卜珝
Bu Xu
37
卜珝，字子玉，匈奴後部人也。 少好讀《易》，郭璞見而歎曰：「吾所弗如也，柰何不免兵厄！ 」珝曰：「然。 吾大厄在四十一，位為卿將，當受禍耳。 不爾者，亦為猛獸所害。 吾亦未見子之令終也。 」璞曰：「吾禍在江南，甚營之，未見免兆。 雖然，在南猶可延期，住此不過時月。 」珝曰：「子勿為公吏，可以免諸。 」璞曰：「吾不能免公吏，猶子之不能免卿將也。 」珝曰：「吾此雖當有帝王子，終不復奉二京矣。 琅邪可奉，卿謹奉之，主晉祀者必此人也。 」珝遂隱于龍門山。 劉元海僭號，徵為大司農、侍中，固以疾辭。 元海曰：「人各有心，卜珝不欲在吾朝，何異高祖四公哉！ 可遂其高志。 」後復徵為光祿大夫，珝謂使者曰：「非吾死所也。 」及劉聰嗣偽位，徵為太常。 時劉琨據并州，聰問何時可平，珝答曰：「并州陛下之分，今茲克之必矣。 」聰戲曰：「朕欲勞先生一行可乎？ 」珝曰：「臣所以來不及裝者，正為是行也。 」聰大悅，署珝使持節、平北將軍。 將行，謂其妹曰：「此行也，死自吾分，後慎勿紛紜。 」及攻晉陽，為琨所敗，珝卒先奔，為其元帥所殺。
Bu Xu, courtesy name Ziyu, belonged to the Xiongnu rear division. While Bu Xu was still a youth poring over the Zhouyi, Guo Pu met him and marveled, "I am not his equal—yet how will he escape dying by the sword?" Bu Xu calmly replied, "It is as you say." He foretold his own doom at forty-one as a minister-general. If not that, a savage beast would kill him. He added that he did not see a peaceful end for Guo Pu either. Guo Pu said his peril lay in the south, with no sign of escape. Bu Xu replied that the south might delay fate, but staying north bought only a few months. He urged Guo Pu never to take a clerk's post if he wished to live. Guo Pu answered that neither could escape the roles fate assigned. Bu Xu predicted an imperial scion would rise yet the two capitals would never be restored under them. He told Guo to cleave to the prince of Langye—the man who would carry the Jin rites. Bu Xu then withdrew to Mount Longmen. Liu Yuan summoned him as grand minister of agriculture; he feigned illness and refused. Liu Yuan compared his refusal to the recluses Han Gaozu could not compel. He let Bu Xu keep his hermit pride. When summoned as supernumerary grandee, he told the envoy that office was not where he would perish. Under Liu Cong he was called to be grand master of ceremonies. When Liu Cong asked when Liu Kun's Bingzhou would fall, Bu Xu said the stars marked it for the barbarian house that very year. Liu Cong teasingly asked him to lead the campaign himself. Bu Xu replied he had hurried north unprepared precisely to accept that march. Delighted, Liu Cong named him credential-bearing commissioner and general who pacifies the north. Before leaving he told his sister the campaign meant his death and bade her not to mourn loudly. At the assault on Jinyang he broke before Liu Kun and was cut down by his own commander for cowardice.
38
鮑靚
Bao Jing
39
鮑靚，字太玄，東海人也。 年五歲，語父母云：「本是曲陽李家兒，九歲墜井死。 」其父母尋訪得李氏，推問皆符驗。 靚學兼內外，明天文河洛書，稍遷南陽中部都尉，為南海太守。 嘗行部入海，遇風，饑甚，取白石煮食之以自濟。 王機時為廣州刺史，入廁，忽見二人著烏衣，與機相捍，良久擒之，得二物似烏鴨。 靚曰：「此物不祥。 」機焚之，徑飛上天，機尋誅死。 靚嘗見仙人陰君，授道訣，百餘歲卒。
Bao Jing, courtesy name Taixuan, came from Donghai commandery. At five he told his parents he had been a Li boy in Quyang who drowned in a well at nine. They traced the Li household and every detail matched his tale. He mastered Confucian and occult lore, astrology, and Hetu-Luoshu numerology, rising to Nanyang commandant and Nanhai governor. Caught in a gale at sea on tour, he boiled white flints for food and survived. When Wang Ji was governor of Guangzhou, he seized two crow-shaped imps that attacked him in the latrine. Bao Jing called them ill omens. Wang Ji burned them; they shot skyward; soon afterward he was executed. He met the immortal Yin Jun, received Dao formulas, and died past the century mark.
40
吳猛
Wu Meng
41
吳猛，豫章人也。 少有孝行，夏日常手不驅蚊，懼其去己而噬親也。 年四十，邑人丁義始授其神方。 因還豫章，江波甚急，猛不假舟楫，以白羽扇畫水而渡，觀者異之。 庾亮為江州刺史，嘗遇疾，聞猛神異，乃迎之，問己疾何如。 猛辭以算盡，請具棺服。 旬日而死，形狀如生。 未及大斂，遂失其屍。 識者以為亮不祥之徵。 亮疾果不起。
Wu Meng was a native of Yuzhang. As a boy he let mosquitoes feed on his own flesh so they would not trouble his parents. At forty Ding Yi of his town taught him an esoteric formula. Returning to Yuzhang he crossed a raging stream by fanning the water with a white feather fan, astonishing onlookers. Yu Liang, as Jiangzhou governor, summoned him when ill to ask his fate. Wu Meng answered that Yu Liang's span was spent and asked him to ready coffin clothes. He died within ten days, yet his corpse looked as though he still lived. Before the encoffining rites could begin, the body had vanished. Knowledgable onlookers read it as a dark portent for Yu Liang. Yu Liang never rose from his sickbed.
42
幸靈
Xing Ling
43
幸靈者，豫章建昌人也。 性少言，與小人群居，見侵辱而無慍色，邑裏號之癡，雖其父母兄弟亦以為癡也。 嘗使守稻，群牛食之，靈見而不驅，待牛去乃往理其殘亂者。 其父母見而怒之，靈曰：「夫萬物生天地之間，各欲得食。 牛方食，柰何驅之！ 」其父愈怒曰：「即如汝言，復用理壞者何為？ 」靈曰：「此稻又欲得終其性，牛自犯之，靈可以不收乎！」
Xing Ling came from Jianchang county in Yuzhang commandery. Taciturn, he lived among common folk, endured abuse without a scowl, and the whole hamlet mocked him as simple—even his kin thought him dull-witted. Set to watch the paddies, he let the oxen finish grazing before he straightened the trampled stalks. His parents scolded him; he answered that every creature under heaven hungered alike. "The herd is feeding—why chase them away?" His father snapped that if that were true, tidying ruined grain was pointless. Ling retorted that the grain still deserved its full growth, the cattle had wronged it, and he was bound to salvage what remained.
44
時順陽樊長賓為建昌令，發百姓作官船於建城山中，吏令人各作箸一雙。 靈作而未輸，或竊之焉。 俄而竊者心痛欲死，靈謂之曰：「爾得無竊我箸乎？ 」竊者不應。 有頃，愈急，靈曰：「若爾不以情告我者，今真死矣。 」竊者急遽，乃首出之。 靈於是飲之以水，病即立愈。 行人由此敬畏之。 船成，當下，吏以二百人引一艘，不能動，方請益人。 靈曰：「此以過足，但部分未至耳。 靈請自牽之。 」乃手執箸，惟用百人，而船去如流。 眾大驚怪，咸稱其神，於是知名。
Fan Changbin of Shunyang, then magistrate of Jianchang, conscripted villagers to build government vessels in the Jiancheng hills and required every laborer to turn in one pair of chopsticks. Xing Ling finished his pair, yet before he could hand them in someone stole them. The thief doubled over with chest pain until Ling asked whether he had lifted the chopsticks. The culprit kept silent. As the agony mounted, Ling warned that only a frank confession would spare him. Panicked, the thief owned up and produced them. Xing Ling gave him water and the pain vanished instantly. Travelers thereafter stood in awe of him. On launch day two hundred haulers could not budge a single hull, so the bailiffs begged for more hands. Ling said the crews were already ample but badly deployed. He volunteered to marshal the tow-ropes himself. Chopsticks in hand, he redeployed a hundred men and the barge glided downstream like swift water. The throng gasped, hailed him a wonder-worker, and his fame spread.
45
有龔仲儒女病積年，氣息財屬，靈使以水含之，已而強起，應時大愈。 又呂猗母皇氏得痿痹病，十有餘年，靈療之，去皇氏數尺而坐，冥目寂然，有頃，顧謂猗曰：「扶夫人令起。 」猗曰：「老人得病累年，奈何可倉卒起邪？ 」靈曰：「但試扶起。 」於是兩人夾扶以立。 少選，靈又令去扶，即能自行，由此遂愈。 於是百姓奔趣，水陸輻輳，從之如雲。 皇氏自以病久，懼有發動，靈乃留水一器令食之，每取水，輒以新水補處，二十餘年水清如新，塵垢不能加焉。
Gong Zhongru's daughter had lain at death's door for years until Ling had her rinse with water; she sat up vigorously and recovered at once. He also healed Lü Yi's mother, crippled by palsy for a decade, by sitting yards away in trance until he told Lü Yi to help her stand. Lü Yi protested that an aged invalid could not be roused in haste. Ling bade him simply try. Two servants braced her upright. Moments later he had them let go, and she walked unaided thereafter. Commoners flocked by river and road until his train swelled like clouds. Fearing relapse, she kept his jar; each draught was topped with fresh water, and for over twenty years the liquid stayed crystal-clear, untainted by grime.
46
時高悝家有鬼怪，言語訶叱，投擲內外，不見人形，或器物自行，再三發火，巫祝厭劾而不能絕。 適值靈，乃要之。 靈於陌頭望其屋，謂悝曰：「此君之家邪？ 」悝曰：「是也。 」靈曰：「知之足矣。 」悝固請之，靈不得已，至門，見符索甚多，謂悝曰：「當以正止邪，而以邪救邪，惡得已乎！ 」並使焚之，惟據軒小坐而去，其夕鬼怪即絕。
Gao Kui's mansion was plagued by bodiless voices, flying crockery, self-moving tools, and fires no exorcist could quell. Meeting Xing Ling by chance, they pressed him to help. From the lane mouth he studied the roofline and asked if it was Gao Kui's house. Gao Kui confirmed it. Ling said knowing that was enough. Dragged to the gate, he saw charms papering the lintel and scolded that chasing fiends with more sorcery could never set things right. He made them burn every charm, lingered briefly on the porch, and left; the haunting ended that very night.
47
靈所救愈多此類，然不取報謝。 行不騎乘，長不娶妻，性至恭，見人即先拜，言輒自名。 凡草木之夭傷于山林者，必起理之，器物之傾覆于途路者，必舉正之。 周旋江州間，謂其士人曰：「天地之於人物，一也，咸欲不失其情性，奈何制服人以為奴婢乎！ 諸君若欲享多福以保性命，可悉免遣之。 」十餘年間，賴其術以濟者極多。 後乃娶妻，畜車以奴婢，受貨賂致遺，於是其術稍衰，所療得失相半焉。
Most of his cures followed this pattern, yet he accepted no fee. He walked everywhere, never wed, bowed before any interlocutor, and introduced himself by name. He straightened wind-snapped saplings in the wild and righted overturned gear on the highway. Ranging Jiangzhou, he lectured local scholars that heaven treated all beings alike and reproached those who enserfed others. He urged them to free every bond servant if they valued long life. For a decade multitudes credited his teaching with deliverance. Later he married, kept carriages and bondsmen, and took bribes; his powers waned and his cures became hit or miss.
48
佛圖澄
Fotucheng
49
佛圖澄，天竺人也。 本姓帛氏。 少學道，妙通玄術。 ，來適洛陽，自雲百有餘歲，常服氣自養，能積日不食。 善誦神咒，能役使鬼神。 腹旁有一孔，常以絮塞之，每夜讀書，則拔絮，孔中出光，照於一室。 又嘗齋時，平旦至流水側，從腹旁孔中引出五藏六府洗之，訖，還內腹中。 又能聽鈴音以言吉凶，莫不懸驗。
The monk Fotucheng hailed from India (Tianzhu). His clan name had been Bo. Trained in Daoist practice from boyhood, he mastered occult skills. He reached Luoyang claiming to exceed a century in age, nourished himself on breath discipline, and could fast for many successive days. He excelled at spirit mantras and could bind ghosts to his will. A cotton-plugged aperture in his flank, uncorked at study time, cast enough radiance to light a chamber. At fasting dawn he once drew his viscera through that opening to rinse them in a stream, then tucked them back inside. He divined by temple bells, and every omen proved true beforehand.
50
及洛中寇亂，乃潛草野以觀變。 石勒屯兵葛陂，專行殺戮，沙門遇害者其眾。 澄投勒大將軍郭黑略家，黑略每從勒征伐，輒豫克勝負，勒疑而問曰：「孤不覺卿有出眾智謀，而每知軍行吉凶何也？ 」黑略曰：「將軍天挺神武，幽靈所助，有一沙門智術非常，雲將軍當略有區夏，己應為師。 臣前後所白，皆其言也。 」勒召澄，試以道術。 澄即取缽盛水，燒香咒之，須臾缽中生青蓮花，光色曜日，勒由此信之。
As Luoyang fell to rebels he withdrew to the wilderness to watch how events would turn. At Gebei Shi Le's army slaughtered mercilessly, and countless monks perished. Fotucheng took refuge with Shi Le's general Guo Heilüe, whose uncanny battlefield forecasts drew Shi Le's question: he saw no genius in Guo—so how did he always read every march? Guo Heilüe credited a strange monk who foretold Shi Le's conquest of the Central Plain and named himself disciple. Every report Guo had made came from the monk. Shi Le summoned Fotucheng and put his thaumaturgy to trial. He filled an alms bowl with water, cursed over incense, and raised azure lotuses whose glare outshone the sun—convincing Shi Le.
51
勒自葛陂還河北，過枋頭，枋頭人夜欲斫營，澄謂黑略曰：「須臾賊至，可令公知。 」果如其言，有備，故不敗。 勒欲試澄，夜冠胄衣甲，執刀而坐，遣人告澄云：「夜來不知大將軍何所在。 」使人始至，未及有言，澄逆問曰：「平居無寇，何故夜嚴？ 」勒益信之。 勒後因忿，欲害諸道士，並欲苦澄。 澄乃潛避至黑略舍，語弟子曰：「若將軍信至，問吾所在者，報雲不知所之。 」既而勒使至，覓澄不得。 使還報勒，勒驚曰：「吾有惡意向澄，澄舍我去矣。 」通夜不寢，思欲見澄。 澄知勒意悔，明旦造勒。 勒曰：「昨夜何行？ 」澄曰：「公有怒心，昨故權避公。 今改意，是以敢來。 勒大笑曰：「道人謬矣。」
Marching homeward past Fangtou, Fotucheng warned Guo Heilüe of a night strike so the warlord could brace his lines. The raid came as foretold, but preparedness averted defeat. Shi Le staged a midnight alert in full armor to test the monk, sending a runner to claim the commander could not be found. Before the envoy could speak, Fotucheng demanded why the camp stood battle-ready when no enemy threatened. Shi Le's trust only deepened. In a fury Shi Le resolved to massacre Daoist adepts and torture Fotucheng too. Fotucheng hid with Guo Heilüe and ordered disciples, if messengers asked, to swear they did not know his whereabouts. Shi Le's men arrived and found him gone. The envoy's report left Shi Le thunderstruck that malice had driven the monk away. He lay awake the night through, longing for Fotucheng. Sensing the warlord's remorse, Fotucheng appeared at dawn. Shi Le asked where he had been the night before. The monk answered that Shi Le's wrath had forced him to step aside. Now that the temper had cooled, he dared return. Shi Le roared with laughter and called him mistaken.
52
襄國城塹水源在城西北五里，其水源暴竭，勒問澄何以致水。 澄曰：「今當敕龍取水。 」乃與弟子法首等數人至故泉源上，坐繩床，燒安息香，咒願數百言。 如此三日，水泫然微流，有一小龍長五六寸許，隨水而來，諸道士競往觀之。 有頃，水大至，隍塹皆滿。
When Xiangguo's ditch-fed spring five li northwest ran dry, Shi Le asked how to refill the works. Fotucheng said he would command a dragon to restore the flow. He led Fashou and a few disciples to the old spring, sat a rope cot, burned frankincense, and recited vows for hundreds of lines. After three days a thin rivulet appeared bearing a dragonlet a few inches long that curious Daoists rushed to see. Soon torrents refilled every moat and trench.
53
鮮卑段末波攻勒，眾甚盛。 勒懼，問澄。 澄曰：「昨日寺鈴鳴雲，明旦食時，當擒段末波。 」勒登城望末波軍，不見前後，失色曰：「末波如此，豈可獲乎！ 」更遣夔安問澄。 澄曰：「已獲末波矣。 」時城北伏兵出，遇末波，執之。 澄勸勒宥末波，遣還本國，勒從之，卒獲其用。
The Xianbei chief Duan Mobo assailed Shi Le with overwhelming numbers. Shi Le, daunted, consulted Fotucheng. Fotucheng cited the monastery bells: by tomorrow's mealtime Duan Mobo would be taken. From the battlements the host stretched beyond sight, and Shi Le blanched—how could such a multitude yield their leader? He sent Kui An back to the monk for reassurance. Fotucheng insisted Duan Mobo was already taken. Northern ambushers sprang up and seized Mobo in the same stroke. Fotucheng persuaded Shi Le to spare Mobo and repatriate him, a mercy that later paid strategic dividends.
54
劉曜遣從弟岳攻勒，勒遣石季龍距之。 嶽敗，退保石梁塢，季龍堅柵守之。 澄在襄國，忽歎曰：「劉嶽可憫！ 」弟子法祚問其故，澄曰「昨日亥時，嶽已敗被執。 」果如所言。
Liu Yao dispatched Liu Yue while Shi Le countered with Shi Hu (Shi Jilong). Liu Yue retreated to the Shiliang stockade ringed by Shi Hu's palisade. Fotucheng in Xiangguo cried out in pity for Liu Yue. Asked why, he said Liu Yue had already fallen captive at the previous night's hai watch. Scouts confirmed every word.
55
及曜自攻洛陽，勒將救之，其群下咸諫以為不可。 勒以訪澄，澄曰：「相輪鈴音云：'秀支替戾岡，僕穀劬禿當。 」此羯語也，秀支，軍也。 替戾岡，出也。 僕谷，劉曜胡位也。 劬禿當，捉也。 此言軍出捉得曜也。 」又令一童子潔齋七日，取麻油合胭脂，躬自研於掌中，舉手示童子，粲然有輝。 童子驚曰：「有軍馬甚眾，見一人長大白晳，以硃絲縛其肘。 」澄曰：「此即曜也。 」勒其悅，遂赴洛距曜，生擒之。
When Liu Yao besieged Luoyang, Shi Le prepared a relief march but every minister called it folly. Consulting Fotucheng, he quoted the stupa bell: "Xiuzhi tiligang, pugu qutu dang." He glossed the phrase as Jie speech: xiuzhi meant "army." The compound tiligang glossed the word for "sally forth" or "issue out." Pugu was the Jie-style epithet for Liu Yao's rank. The phrase qutu dang meant "to seize" or "to take captive." Taken together, the oracle meant the host would march out and take Liu Yao alive. He had a novice fast seven days, blend sesame oil with rouge in his own palm, then lift his hand before the boy until it shone dazzling bright. The boy cried out that he saw endless squadrons and a towering, pale figure with crimson cords about his forearm. Fotucheng said, "That man is Liu Yao." Shi Le rejoiced, marched on Luoyang to meet Liu Yao, and took him prisoner alive.
56
勒僭稱趙天王，行皇帝事，敬澄彌篤。 時石蔥將叛，澄誡勒曰：「今年蔥中有蟲，食必害人，可令百姓無食蔥也。 」勒班告境內，慎無食蔥。 俄而石蔥果走。 勒益重之，事必諮而後行，號曰大和尚。
Having arrogated the style Heavenly King of Zhao while wielding imperial power, Shi Le honored Fotucheng more devotedly than before. When Shi Cong plotted revolt, Fotucheng punned on the word "scallion" (cong) and warned Shi Le that "scallions" harbored worms—so the realm should shun them. Shi Le issued an edict forbidding the people to touch scallions. Soon afterward Shi Cong bolted, as foretold. Shi Le weighted him still higher, took counsel before every move, and addressed him as the Great Monk.
57
勒愛子斌暴病死，將殯，勒歎曰：「朕聞虢太子死，扁鵲能生之，今可得效乎？ 」乃令告澄。 澄取楊枝沾水，灑而咒之。 就執斌手曰：「可起矣！ 」因此遂蘇，有頃，平復。 自是勒諸子多在澄寺中養之。 勒死之年，天靜無風，而塔上一鈴獨鳴，澄謂眾曰：「鈴音雲，國有大喪，不出今年矣。 」既而勒果死。
When his favorite son Shi Bin died suddenly on the eve of obsequies, Shi Le mourned aloud whether any healer could work Bian Que's miracle for the dead. He sent word to Fotucheng. Fotucheng dipped a willow spray in water, sprinkled the corpse, and intoned spells. He seized Shi Bin's hand and commanded him to rise. The prince stirred and within moments seemed wholly recovered. Afterward most of Shi Le's sons were raised inside Fotucheng's temple. The year Shi Le died, though the air was breathless, a lone stupa bell tolled; Fotucheng told the monks it portended a court bereavement before year's end. Shi Le soon followed.
58
及季龍僭位，遷都於鄴，傾心事澄，有重於勒。 下書衣澄以綾錦，乘以雕輦，朝會之日，引之升殿，常侍以下悉助舉輿，太子諸公扶翼而上，主者唱大和尚，眾坐皆起，以彰其尊。 又使司空李農旦夕親問，其太子諸公五日一朝，尊敬莫與為比。 支道林在京師，聞澄與諸石遊，乃曰：「澄公其以季龍為海鷗鳥也。 百姓因澄故多奉佛，皆營造寺廟，相競出家，真偽混淆，多生愆過。 季龍下書料簡，其著作郎王度奏曰：「佛，外國之神，非諸華所應祠奉。 漢代初傳其道，惟聽西域人得立寺都邑，以奉其神，漢人皆不出家。 魏承漢制，亦循前軌。 今可斷趙人悉不聽詣寺燒香禮拜，以遵典禮，其百辟卿士下逮眾隸，例皆禁之，其有犯者，與淫祀同罪。 其趙人為沙門者，還服百姓。 」朝士多同度所奏。 季龍以澄故，下書曰：「朕出自邊戎，忝君諸夏，至於饗祀，應從本俗。 佛是戎神，所應兼奉，其夷趙百姓有樂事佛者，特聽之。」
After Shi Hu (Shi Jilong) seized the throne and shifted the seat to Ye, he lavished attention on Fotucheng beyond even Shi Le's devotion. Edicts robed the monk in silk, gave him a carved litter, and on audience days convoked him to the dais with ministers hoisting his chair and princes flanking him while criers hailed the Great Monk so that every official stood. Minister of Works Li Nong attended him daily, while the heir and nobles presented themselves every fifth day—no one else enjoyed such deference. Zhi Daolin in the capital, learning that Fotucheng walked among the Shi clan, remarked that the master must treat Shi Hu as the heedless gull of the fable. On his account the populace turned fervently Buddhist, racing to found cloisters and tonsure until authentic practice blurred with sham and abuses multiplied. Shi Hu ordered a review; Editorial Director Wang Du argued that the Buddha was a foreign deity unfit for Chinese state cult. At the Han introduction only Westerners could build urban monasteries, while native Chinese were barred from ordination. Wei continued Han precedent on the same footing. He urged that Zhao subjects be forbidden temples, incense, and prostration to honor classical rites, extending the ban from high ministers to common laborers on pain of illicit-cult penalties. Any Zhao monk should be laicized. Most courtiers sided with Wang Du. Yet Shi Hu, for Fotucheng's sake, proclaimed his barbarian origins and insisted ancestral rites follow steppe custom. The Buddha, he wrote, was a frontier deity worthy of joint worship, and any Zhao or tribesman who wished to serve him might do so.
59
澄時止鄴城寺中，弟子遍于郡國。 嘗遣弟子法常北至襄國，弟子法佐從襄國還，相遇于梁基城下，對車夜談，言及和尚，比旦各去。 佐始入，澄逆笑曰：「昨夜爾與法常交車共說汝師邪？ 」佐愕然愧懺。 於是國人每相語：「莫起噁心，和尚知汝。 」及澄之所在，無敢向其方面涕唾者。
Fotucheng resided in the Ye temple while disciples spread through every province. He once dispatched Fachang north to Xiangguo while Fazuo returned south; the two met below Liangji, spoke in their carriages until dawn of their master, then parted. As Fazuo entered, Fotucheng laughed that he had overheard their midnight colloquy about him. Fazuo froze, then blushed with contrition. Henceforth folk whispered that no ill thought escaped the monk's ken. None dared face his quarters to spit or weep.
60
季龍太子邃有二字，在襄國，澄語邃曰：「小阿彌比當得疾，可往看之。 」邃即馳信往視，果已得疾。 太醫殷騰及外國道士自言能療之。 澄告弟子法牙曰：「正使聖人復出，不愈此疾，況此等乎！ 」後三日果死。 邃將圖為逆，謂內豎曰：「和尚神通，儻發吾謀。 明日來者，當先除之。 」澄月望將入覲季龍，謂弟子僧慧曰：「昨夜天神呼我曰：'明日若入，還勿過人。 」我儻有所過，汝當止我。 」澄常入，必過邃。 邃知澄入，要侯甚苦。 澄將上南台，僧慧引衣，澄曰：「事不得止。 」坐未安便起，邃固留不住，所謀遂差。 還寺，歎曰：「太子作亂，其形將成，欲言難言，欲忍難忍。 」乃因事從容箴季龍，季龍終不能解。 俄而事發，方悟澄言。
Shi Hu's heir Shi Sui had two boys in Xiangguo; Fotucheng warned him the younger would sicken and bade him visit. Shi Sui sent riders at once and found the child already stricken. Palace physician Yin Teng and foreign adepts claimed they could heal him. Fotucheng told Faya that neither sages nor charlatans could save the boy. Three days later the child was dead. Shi Sui plotted revolt and muttered to eunuchs that Fotucheng's clairvoyance might expose him. He ordered tomorrow's visitors killed beforehand. On the day of audience Fotucheng warned Seng Hui that a spirit had forbidden him to "pass others" inside the palace. If he should cross someone's path, the disciple must check him. His usual route always crossed Shi Sui's quarters. Shi Sui lay in desperate wait along that corridor. As he climbed the south terrace Seng Hui tugged his robe, but Fotucheng said the summons could not be refused. He barely sat down, then rose and slipped Shi Sui's grasp, foiling the ambush. Back at the cloister he groaned that the heir's mutiny was ripening yet could neither be told outright nor silently borne. He circled the warning obliquely, but Shi Hu never grasped it. When the plot erupted, Shi Hu finally saw his meaning.
61
後郭黑略將兵征長安北山羌，墮羌伏中。 時澄在堂上坐，慘然改容曰：「郭公今有厄。 」乃唱云：「眾僧祝願。 」澄又自祝願。 須臾，更曰：若東南出者活，余向者則困。 」復更祝願。 有頃，曰：「脫矣。 」後月餘，黑略還，自說墜羌圍中，東南走，馬乏，正遇帳下人，推馬與之曰：「公乘此馬，小人乘公馬，濟與不濟，命也。 」略得其馬，故獲免。 推檢時日，正是澄祝願時也。
Later Guo Heilüe campaigned against the northern-shan Qiang near Chang'an and walked into an ambush. Fotucheng, seated in the refectory, blanched and cried that Guo Heilüe was in mortal peril. He called for the community to pray. Then he prayed himself. Moments later he amended the omen: escape southeast meant life; other headings meant doom. He prayed again. Soon he announced deliverance. A month later Guo Heilüe returned, telling how he broke southeast, foundered, and a retainer swapped mounts, saying survival was heaven's whim. That remount won him his life. The timestamps matched Fotucheng's prayers exactly.
62
時天旱，季龍遣其太子詣臨漳西滏口祈雨，久而不降，乃令澄自行，即有白龍二頭降於祠所，其日大雨方數千里。 澄嘗遣弟子向西域市香，既行，澄告余弟子曰：「掌中見買香弟子在某處被劫垂死。 」因燒香祝願，遙救護之。 弟子後還，雲某月某日某處為賊所劫，垂當見殺，忽聞香氣，賊無故自驚曰：「救兵已至。 」棄之而走。 黃河中舊不生黿，時有得者，以獻季龍。 澄見而之曰：「桓溫入河，其不久乎！ 」溫字元子，後果如其言也。 季龍嘗晝寢，夢見群羊負魚從東北來，寤以訪澄。 澄曰：「不祥也，鮮卑其有中原乎！ 」後亦皆驗。 澄嘗與季龍升中台，澄忽驚曰：「變，變，幽州當火災。 」乃取酒噀之，久而笑曰：「救已得矣。 」季龍遣驗幽州，雲爾日火從四門起，西南有黑雲來，驟雨滅之，雨亦頗有酒氣。
During a drought Shi Hu first sent the heir to pray at Fukou west of Linzhang, then Fotucheng himself; two white dragons alighted on the altar and rain swept thousands of li. When monks went west for incense, Fotucheng told those behind that vision showed the buyer ambushed and dying. He burned incense and sent a distant deliverance. The monk returned reporting that robbers had stayed his execution until they smelled incense and fled, crying that reinforcements had come. They dropped him and bolted. Yellow River turtles were unheard of until one was caught and sent to Shi Hu. Fotucheng declared the omen meant Huan Wen would soon ford the Yellow River. Huan Wen, styled Yuanzi, did exactly as he foretold. Shi Hu dreamed sheep laden with fish from the northeast and asked Fotucheng on waking. Fotucheng called it ill-omened: the Xianbei would take the heartland. Later events bore him out. On the central tower he suddenly cried that Youzhou faced a great blaze. He spat wine into the air, then laughed that the danger was averted. Inspectors reported flames bursting from Youzhou's gates until black clouds and a reeking downpour—almost vinous—doused them.
63
石宣將殺石韜，宣先到寺與澄同坐，浮屠一鈴獨鳴，澄謂曰：「解鈴音乎？ 鈴雲鬍子洛度。 」宣變色曰：「是何言歟？ 」澄謬曰：「老胡為道，不能山居無言，重茵美服，豈非洛度乎！ 」石韜後至，澄孰視良久。 韜懼而問澄，澄曰：「怪公血臭，故相視耳。 」季龍夢龍飛西南，自天而落，旦而問澄，澄曰：「禍將作矣，宜父子慈和，深以慎之。 」季龍引澄入東閣，與其後杜氏問訊之。 澄曰：「脅下有賊，不出十日，自浮圖以西，此殿以東，當有血流，慎勿東也。 」杜後曰：「和尚耄邪！ 何處有賊？ 」澄即易語云：「六情所受，皆悉是賊。 老自應耄，但使少者不昏即好耳。 」遂便寓言，不復彰的。 後二日，宣果遣人害韜於佛寺中，欲因季龍臨喪殺之。 季龍以澄先誡，故獲免。 及宣被收，澄諫季龍曰：「皆陛下之子也，何為重禍邪！ 陛下若含怒加慈者，尚有六十餘歲。 如必誅之，宣當為彗星下掃鄴宮。 」季龍不從。 後月餘，有一妖馬，髦尾皆有燒狀，入中陽門，出顯陽門，東首東宮，皆不得入，走向東北，俄爾不見。 澄聞而歎曰：「災其及矣！ 」季龍大享群臣于太武前殿，澄吟曰：「殿乎，殿乎！ 棘子成林，將壞人衣。 」季龍令發殿石下視之，有棘生焉。 冉閔小字棘奴。
Before Shi Xuan murdered Shi Tao he sat with Fotucheng while a lone bell tolled; the monk asked if he grasped its message. The bell, he said, meant "the bearded man fords the river"—a Jie gloss on the plot. Shi Xuan flushed and demanded what he meant. Fotucheng feigned to mock his own luxury as a monk who could not keep mountain silence. When Shi Tao entered, Fotucheng studied him at length. Shi Tao quailed; Fotucheng said only that he smelled blood on him. Shi Hu dreamed a dragon plummet from the sky; Fotucheng warned of coming woe and urged father-son harmony. Shi Hu brought him to the east gallery for Empress Du to question. He warned of assassins within ten days, blood west of the stupa and east of the hall, and bade them shun the eastern precincts. Empress Du sneered that the monk was senile. She asked where brigands could hide. Fotucheng pivoted, saying every passion was a robber of the mind. He granted his own dotage if only the young stayed clear-headed. He dropped explicit prophecy and spoke in parables. Two days later Shi Xuan had Shi Tao murdered in a monastery, planning to strike Shi Hu at the obsequies. Forewarned by Fotucheng, Shi Hu escaped the trap. When Shi Xuan was seized, Fotucheng begged Shi Hu not to compound the tragedy among his sons. Mercy, he said, could yet extend Shi Hu's life sixty-some years. If Shi Xuan were put to death, a comet would scour the Ye palaces—so he warned. Shi Hu refused the plea. A month later a spectral horse with burnt mane and tail galloped from Zhongyang to Xianyang gate, wheeled toward the Eastern Palace yet could not enter, then fled northeast and vanished. Hearing the news, Fotucheng sighed, "Disaster is upon us! Shi Hu feasted his ministers before the Hall of Martial Might; Fotucheng chanted, "The hall—alas, the hall! Brambles have grown into a thicket—they will shred men's garments." Shi Hu had workmen pry up the foundation stones and found thorns sprouting underneath. Ran Min's pet name had been "Slave of the Thorns."
64
季龍造太武殿初成，圖畫自古賢聖、忠臣、孝子、烈士、貞女，皆變為胡狀，旬餘，頭悉縮入肩中，惟冠䯰仿佛微出，季龍大惡之，秘而不言也。 澄對之流涕，乃自啟塋墓於鄴西紫陌，還寺，獨語曰：「得三年乎？ 」自答：「不得。 」又曰：「得二年、一年、百日、一月乎？ 」自答：「不得。 」遂無復言。 謂弟子法祚曰：「戊申歲禍亂漸萌，己酉石氏當滅。 吾及其未亂，先從化矣。 」卒于鄴宮寺。 後有沙門從雍州來，稱見澄西入關，季龍掘而視之，惟有一石無屍。 季龍惡之曰：「石者，朕也，葬我而去，吾將死矣。 」因而遇疾。 明年，季龍死，遂大亂。
When Shi Hu finished the new Hall of Martial Might, every fresco of ancient sages, loyal ministers, filial sons, martyrs, and chaste wives morphed into steppe faces; within a fortnight the heads had sunk into the shoulders so that only the hats and hair-knots peeked forth. Shi Hu was revolted but told no one. Fotucheng wept at the sight, chose his own tomb west of Ye on Purple Road, returned to the cloister, and muttered, "Will I get three years? He answered himself: "No." "Two years? A year? A hundred days? A month? "No." He fell silent. To his disciple Fazuo he said, "Strife will stir in the wushen year, and the House of Shi will fall in jiyou. I shall quit this life before the storm breaks." He passed away in the imperial monastery at Ye. Later a monk from Yongzhou swore he had seen Fotucheng riding west through the passes; Shi Hu opened the grave and found only a slab of stone—no body. Shi Hu took it ill: "'Stone' is me—he buried his token and walked away—I am dying! He fell ill on the spot. The following year Shi Hu died, and the realm collapsed into chaos.
65
麻襦
Ma Ru
66
麻襦者，不知何許人也，莫得其姓名。 石季龍時，在魏縣市中乞丐，恆著麻襦布裳，故時人謂之麻襦。 言語卓越，狀如狂者，乞得米穀不食，輒散置大路，雲飴天馬。 趙興太守籍狀收送詣季龍。
The man called "Hemp Cloak"—no one knew his origin or his real name. Under Shi Hu he begged in the Wei county marketplace, always dressed in a homespun hemp jacket, hence the nickname. He spoke in lofty riddles like a man possessed; the grain he received he never ate but strewed across the highway, claiming he was foddering heaven's horses. The prefect of Zhao-xing had him arrested on the rolls and escorted him to Shi Hu.
67
先是，佛圖澄謂季龍曰：「國東二百里某月日當送一非常人，勿殺之也。 」如期果至。 季龍與共語，了無異言，惟道：「陛下當終一柱殿下。 」季龍不解，送以詣澄。 麻襦謂澄曰：「昔在光和中會，奄至今日。 酉戎受玄命，絕曆終有期。 金離消于壞，邊荒不能遵，驅除靈期跡，莫已已之懿。 裔苗葉繁，其來方積。 休期於何期，永以歎之。 」澄曰：「天回運極，否將不支，九木水為難，無可以術寧。 玄哲雖存世，莫能基必莫能基必頹。 久游閻浮利，擾擾多此患。 行登陵雲宇，會于虛遊間。 」其所言人莫能曉。 季龍遣驛馬送還本縣，既出城，請步，云：「我當有所過，君至合口橋見待。 」使人如言而馳，至橋，麻襦已先至。
Earlier Fotucheng had warned Shi Hu, "On such-and-such a day, two hundred li east of your capital, an extraordinary man will arrive—do not execute him. He arrived exactly as foretold. Shi Hu spoke with him; he offered nothing remarkable except: "Your Majesty will die beneath a one-pillar hall. Puzzled, Shi Hu sent him on to Fotucheng. Ma Ru told Fotucheng, "We met at the Zhonghui assembly in the Guanghe era—now suddenly we stand in this age. The Shi host receives the hidden mandate; the dynasty's span is fixed and its end is timed. Metal melts in the ruin; the frontiers will not hold order; fate's footprints are swept away—nothing can halt its awful closure. Sprigs leaf thickly; the onrush has only begun to mass. When rests the appointed time—if ever? I sigh without end. Fotucheng replied, "The cosmic cycle has turned; decline cannot be propped up; wood and water among the stems spell disaster—no rite can quiet it. Sages walk among us still, yet none can buttress what is bound to fall. Long have we roamed Jambudvipa; turmoil heaps such grief upon us. We shall climb the tower that brushes the clouds and rendezvous in the emptiness between wanderings. No one could fathom his words. Shi Hu sent him home by relay; outside the walls he insisted on walking, saying, "I have an errand—meet me at Forkmouth Bridge. The runner spurred on as bid yet found Ma Ru waiting when he reached the span.
68
後慕容俊投季龍屍于漳水，倚橋柱不流，時人以為「一柱殿下」即謂此也。 及元帝嗣位江左，亦以為「天馬」之應云。
Later Murong Jun threw Shi Hu's body into the Zhang—where it snagged on a bridge pier and refused to float; folk then saw the prophecy of the "one-pillar hall" in that very pier. When Emperor Yuan took the throne south of the Yangzi, courtiers likewise cited it as proof of the "heavenly horses" omen.
69
單道開
Shan Daokai
70
單道開，敦煌人也。 常衣粗褐，或贈以繒服，皆不著，不畏寒暑，晝夜不臥。 恆服細石子，一吞數枚，日一服，或多或少。 好山居，而山樹諸神見異形試之，初無懼色。 石季龍時，從西平來，一日行七百里，其一沙彌年十四，行亦及之。 至秦州，表送到鄴，季龍令佛圖澄與語，不能屈也。 初止鄴城西沙門法綝祠中，後徙臨漳昭德寺。 于房內造重閣，高八九尺，于上編管為禪室，常坐其中。 季龍資給甚厚，道開皆以施人。 人或來諮問者，道開都不答。 日服鎮守藥數丸，大如梧子，藥有松蜜姜桂伏苓之氣，時復飲荼蘇一二升而已。 自雲能療目疾，就療者頗驗。 視其行動，狀若有神。 佛圖澄曰：「此道士觀國興衰，若去者，當有大亂。 」及季龍末，道開南渡許昌，尋而鄴中大亂。
Shan Daokai came from Dunhuang. He always wore burlap rejects; silks offered him went unworn; heat and cold never troubled him, and he never slept by day or night. He swallowed several small stones each day, in greater or lesser number. He preferred hermitage in the hills; genii of grove and crag shifted shape to test him, yet he never flinched. Under Shi Hu he marched from Xiping seven hundred li in a single day; a fourteen-year-old novice matched his pace. Local officials memorialized and sent him to Ye; Shi Hu set Fotucheng to debate him and neither could break the other. First he stayed at Monk Fachin's sanctuary west of Ye, then moved to Zhaode Monastery at Linzhang. Within his room he raised a loft eight or nine feet high, lattice-wove canes into a meditation cell at the top, and habitually sat there. Shi Hu lavished stipends on him, yet he passed every gift to the needy. Questioners who sought counsel received no reply. He swallowed a few wutong-sized "steadying" pills each day—scented of pine honey, ginger, cinnamon, and poria—and occasionally drank a liter or two of herb broth, nothing more. He claimed he could heal the eyes, and patients often went away cured. His gait and manner looked almost otherworldly. Fotucheng said, "This adept reads the kingdom's fate; should he depart, great upheaval will follow. Toward Shi Hu's end Shan Daokai crossed south to Xuchang; chaos soon engulfed Ye.
71
至京師，後至南海，入羅浮山，獨處茅茨，蕭然物外。 年百餘歲，卒於山舍，敕弟子以屍置石穴中，弟子乃移入石室。 陳郡袁宏為南海太守，與弟穎叔及沙門支法防共登羅浮山，至石室口，見道開形骸如生，香火瓦器猶存。 宏曰：「法師業行殊群，正當如蟬蛻耳。 」乃為之贊雲。
He went to the capital, then to the southern sea, withdrew to Mount Luofu, and lived alone in a brush hut, utterly beyond worldly dust. He lived past a century and died in his mountain lodge, commanding disciples to lay his body in a rock hollow; they laid him in a stone cell instead. Yuan Hong of Chen, serving as South Sea prefect, climbed Luofu with his brother Yingshu and Monk Zhi Fafang; at the mouth of the stone cell they found Shan Daokai's corpse lifelike, incense bowls still in place. Yuan Hong said, "The master's vocation set him apart—surely this is the cast-off husk of a cicada. He therefore composed a verse in his honor.
72
黃泓
Huang Hong
73
黃泓，字始長，魏郡斥丘人也。 父沈，善天文秘術。 泓從父受業，精妙逾深，兼博覽經史，尤明《禮》《易》。 性忠勤，非禮不動。 永嘉之亂，與渤海高瞻避地幽州，說瞻曰：「王浚昏暴，終必無成，宜思去就以圖久安。 慕容廆法政修明，虛懷引納，且讖言真人出東北，儻或是乎？ 宜相與歸之，同建事業。 」瞻不從。 泓乃率宗族歸廆，廆待以客禮，引為參軍，軍國之務動輒訪之。 泓指說成敗，事皆如言。 廆常曰：「黃參軍，孤之仲翔也。 」及皝嗣位，遷左常侍，領史官，甚重之。 石季龍攻皝，皝將走遼東，泓曰：「賊有敗氣，無可憂也，不過二日，必當奔潰。 宜嚴勒士馬，為追擊之備。 」皝曰：「今寇盛如此，卿言必走，孤未敢信。 」泓曰：「殿下言盛者，人事耳，臣言必走者，天時也，胡足為疑！ 」及期，季龍果退，皝益奇之。
Huang Hong, courtesy name Shizhang, was a native of Chiqiu in Wei commandery. His father Huang Shen excelled at astronomy and occult techniques. Huang Hong learned from his father, surpassing him in subtlety, and broad reading made him a master of the Book of Rites and Book of Changes. Loyal and diligent by temperament, he never stirred without propriety. When Yongjia's wars scattered the realm, he fled with Gao Zhan of Bohai to Youzhou and warned him, "Wang Jun is violent and foolish—nothing lasting can come of him; weigh whether to stay or leave if you seek peace. Murong Hui governs with clarity, welcomes talent openly, and omens place the "true man" in the northeast—could that be he? Let us both go to him and build something lasting together." Gao Zhan refused. Huang Hong led his kinsmen to Murong Hui, who honored him as a guest, named him staff adviser, and sought his counsel on every civil and military matter. His forecasts of victory and defeat came true every time. Murong Hui often said, "Counselor Huang is my Yu Fan." When Murong Huang succeeded, Huang Hong rose to Left Regular Attendant and chief historiographer, deeply trusted. When Shi Hu struck Murong Huang, who prepared to bolt for Liaodong, Huang Hong said, "The enemy already wears defeat—worry not; within two days they will rout themselves. Muster your troops for a hard pursuit. Murong Huang replied, "The invaders are overwhelming—how can I trust talk of their flight? Huang Hong answered, "Your Highness sees their strength in human terms; I see their rout in heaven's sign—what room for doubt! On schedule Shi Hu retreated, and Murong Huang prized him the more.
74
及慕容俊即王位，遷從事中郎，儁聞冉閔亂，將圖中原，訪之於泓，泓勸行，儁從之。 及僭號，署為進謀將軍、太史令、關內侯，尋加奉車都尉、西海太守、領太史令、開陽亭侯，又封平舒縣五等伯，常從左右，諮決大事，靈台令許敦害其寵，諂事慕容評，設異議以毀之，及以泓為太史靈台諸署統，加給事中。 泓待敦彌厚，不以毀己易心。 慕容暐敗，以老歸家，歎曰：「燕必中興，其在吳王，恨吾年過不見耳。 」年九十七卒。 卒後三年，偽吳王慕容垂興焉。
When Murong Jun took the throne, Huang Hong became palace secretary; learning of Ran Min's revolt, Murong Jun planned a push into the Central Plain, asked Huang Hong, accepted his counsel to march, and acted on it. After Murong Jun claimed the throne, Huang Hong received a string of posts—general of forward counsel, grand astrologer, marquis within the passes—soon augmented by commandant of the imperial carriage, West Sea governor while still astrologer, Kaiting precinct nobleman, and fifth-rank baron of Pingshu; he stayed at the ruler's elbow advising state policy. Lingtai chief Xu Dun resented his favor, curried Murong Ping's goodwill, and carped against him until the court consolidated Huang Hong's observatory and astrologer duties and added palace secretary to his title. Huang Hong treated Xu Dun with greater kindness and let no slander shake him. After Murong Wei's defeat he went home in old age and sighed, "Yan will rise again under the Prince of Wu—I only regret my years will not last to see it. He died at ninety-seven. Three years later the "Prince of Wu," Murong Chui, restored the Yan cause as predicted.
75
索紞
Suo Dan
76
索紞，字叔徹，敦煌人也。 少游京師，受業太學，博綜經籍，遂為通儒。 明陰陽天文，善術數占侯。 司徒辟，除郎中，知中國將亂，避世而歸。 鄉人從紞占問吉凶，門中如市，紞曰：「攻乎異端，戒在害己； 無為多事，多事多患。 」遂詭言虛說，無驗乃止。 惟以占夢為無悔吝，乃不逆問者。
Suo Dan, courtesy name Shuche, was from Dunhuang. He studied at the capital's Imperial Academy in youth, mastered the canon, and became an erudite Confucian. He was adept at yin-yang lore, astronomy, numerology, and omen reading. The minister summoned him to a gentleman post, but foreseeing turmoil in the heartland he resigned and went home. Villagers swarmed his door for divination until it looked like a market. Suo Dan said, "The Analects warn against heterodox pursuits—they ruin the seeker; Meddling breeds trouble; trouble breeds disaster." He therefore fed them nonsense until lack of results cooled their zeal. Only dream interpretation carried no ill omen for the client, so he never turned such callers away.
77
孝廉令狐策夢立冰上，與冰下人語。 紞曰：「冰上為陽，冰下為陰，陰陽事也。 士如歸妻，迨冰未泮，婚姻事也。 君在冰上與冰下人語，為陽語陰，媒介事也。 君當為人作媒，冰泮而婚成。 」策曰：「老夫耄矣，不為媒也。 」會太守田豹因策為子求鄉人張公徵女，仲春而成婚焉。 郡主簿張宅夢走馬上山，還繞舍三周，但見松柏，不知門處。 紞曰：「馬屬離，離為火。 火，禍也。 人上山，為凶字。 但見松伯，墓門象也。 不知門處，為無門也。 三周，三期也。 後三年必有大禍。 」宅果以謀反伏誅。 索充初夢天上有二棺落充前，紞曰：「棺者，職也，當有京師貴人舉君。 二官者，頻再遷。 」俄而司徒王戎書屬太守使舉充，太守先署充功曹而舉孝廉。 充後夢見一虜，脫上衣來詣充。 紞曰：「虜去上中，下半男字，夷狄陰類，君婦當生男。 」終如其言。 宋桷夢內中有一人著赤衣，桷手把兩杖，極打之。 紞曰：「內中有人，肉字也。 肉色，赤也。 兩杖，箸象也。 極打之，飽肉食也。 」俄而亦驗焉。 黃平問紞曰：「我昨夜夢舍中馬舞，數十人向馬拍手，此何祥也？ 」紞曰：「馬者，火也，舞為火起。 向馬拍手，救火人也。 」平未歸而火作。 索綏夢東有二角書詣綏，大角朽敗，小角有題韋囊角佩，一在前，一在後。 紞曰：「大角朽敗，腐棺木。 小角有題，題所詣。 一在前，前紞凶也。 一在後，後背也。 當有凶背之問。 」時綏父在東，居三日而凶問至。 郡功曹張邈嘗奉使詣州，夜夢狼啖一腳。 紞曰：「腳肉被啖，為卻字。 」會東虜反，遂不行。 凡所占莫不驗。
The candidate Linghu Ce dreamed he stood on the ice talking to a man below. Suo Dan said, "Ice above is yang, water below is yin—this is the encounter of yin and yang. As the Book of Songs says of the groom crossing the ford before the ice melts, this speaks of betrothal. You, yang on the surface, speak with yin below—a go-between's work. You will broker another's marriage, and the wedding will conclude when the ice breaks up." Linghu Ce replied that he was too old to broker weddings. Prefect Tian Bao then used Linghu Ce as intermediary to win Zhang Gongzheng's daughter for his son, and the pair wed that mid-spring. Chief Clerk Zhang Zhai dreamed of a horse charging uphill, cantering three circuits around his home amid evergreens, with no doorway in sight. Suo Dan said the horse stood for the trigram li, and li meant fire. Fire portended disaster. Man plus mountain spelled the character for ill omen. Seeing only evergreens evoked a cemetery gate. The missing gate meant there would be no escape. Three rounds foretold three years. A major catastrophe would strike within three years. Zhang Zhai was later put to death for treason, as foretold. Suo Chong dreamed twin coffins drop from heaven; Suo Dan read "coffin" as high office and predicted a metropolitan patron would nominate him. Two coffins meant two successive advancements. Wang Rong soon wrote the prefect, who first named Suo Chong merit clerk and then raised him as filial-incorrupt. Suo Chong later dreamed a tribesman doff his jacket and approach him. Suo Dan parsed the "barbarian" glyph: remove the middle stroke of shang and the lower half reads "male," so a foreign yin omen meant his wife would deliver a boy. The birth matched his reading exactly. Song Que dreamed a red-clad intruder in the women's quarters whom he struck with twin rods. Suo Dan said "person within inner rooms" formed the character for flesh. Flesh implied crimson garb. Twin sticks stood for chopsticks. The beating meant feasting on meat until full. The dream soon proved true. Huang Ping asked Suo Dan about a dream of capering horses and a crowd applauding them indoors. Suo Dan said horses signified fire, and dancing meant flames mounting. Applauding the steeds depicted firefighters at work. A blaze erupted before Huang Ping reached his door. Suo Sui dreamed two horn-marked writs arrive from the east, one decayed, one inscribed, with a tagged pouch and one horn leading, one trailing. The crumbling great horn stood for rotten coffin wood. The smaller horn's text marked where the blow would fall. The foremost placement spelled personal misfortune for Suo Dan. The rear position read as "contrary," a breach of taboo. He foresaw news tied to that reversal. Suo Sui's father was eastward; within three days mourning news came. Merit clerk Zhang Miao, traveling to the provincial seat, dreamed a wolf chewed his foot. Suo Dan read gnawed foot-flesh as the character for retreat. Eastern tribes rose in revolt, so the journey was canceled. Every omen he read came true.
78
太守陰澹從求占書，紞曰：「昔入太學，因一父老為主人，其人無所不知，又匿姓名，有似隱者，紞因從父老問占夢之術，希申鄙藝，審測而說，實無書也。 」澹命為西閣祭酒，紞辭曰：「少無山林之操，遊學京師，交結時賢，會中國不靖，欲養志終年。 老亦至矣，不求聞達。 又少不習勤，老無吏幹，濛汜之年，弗敢聞命。 」澹以束帛禮之，月致羊酒。 年七十五，卒於家。
Prefect Yin Dan asked for written manuals; Suo Dan swore he had learned dream lore from an anonymous sage at the academy and owned no texts, only tested judgment. Yin Dan named him west-pavilion libationer, but Suo Dan refused, citing no hermit vocation, capital schooling, and a wish to retire quietly amid turmoil. He added that old age had come and he craved no fame. He pleaded no talent for administration and declined office in his declining years. The prefect instead sent silk bundles and monthly provisions of mutton and wine. Suo Dan died at home aged seventy-five.
79
孟欽
Meng Qin
80
孟欽，洛陽人也。 有左慈、劉根之術，百姓惑而赴之。 苻堅召詣長安，惡其惑眾，命苻融誅之。 俄而欽至，融留之，遂大宴郡僚，酒酣，目左右收欽。 欽化為旋風，飛出第外。 頃之，有告在城東者，融遣騎追之，垂及，忽然已遠，或有兵眾距戰，或前有溪澗，騎不得過，遂不知所在。 堅未，復見於青州。 苻朗尋之，入於海島。
Meng Qin came from Luoyang. He wielded thaumaturgy like Zuo Ci and Liu Gen, drawing credulous crowds. Fu Jian called him to Chang'an, loathed his sway over the populace, and told Fu Rong to kill him. Meng Qin appeared; Fu Rong detained him, wined his officials, then signaled guards to arrest him mid-banquet. Meng Qin became a whirlwind and shot past the manor walls. Riders chased reports east of town, but phantoms of armies and gorges kept them from closing in, and he vanished. Late in Fu Jian's rule he resurfaced in Qingzhou. Fu Lang tracked him to a sea isle and lost him there.
81
王嘉
Wang Jia
82
王嘉，字子年，隴西安陽人也。 輕舉止，醜形貌，外若不足，而聰睿內明。 滑稽好語笑，不食五穀，不衣美麗，清虛服氣，不與世人交遊。 隱于東陽穀，鑿崖穴居，弟子受業者數百人，亦皆穴處。 石季龍之末，棄其徒眾，至長安，潛隱於終南山，結庵廬而止。 門人聞而復隨之，乃遷於倒獸山。 苻堅累徵不起，公侯已下咸躬往參詣，好尚之士無不師宗之。 問其當世事者，皆隨問而對。 好為譬喻，狀如戲調； 言未然之事，辭如讖記，當時鮮能曉之，事過皆驗。
Wang Jia, courtesy Zinian, hailed from Anyang in Longxi. He seemed slovenly and homely yet was razor-sharp inside.
